title: Sabbat of the Witch Kansai ending
titleJa: サノバウィッチ 聖地巡礼（京都・大阪・神戸）
summary: Sabbat of the Witch (Yuzusoft, an Osaka company) uses real places in Kyoto, Osaka and Kobe, not the Tokyo area. Fly Sapporo/Asahikawa to Osaka on day 13, see Kyoto (station, the school model at Kyoto Concert Hall, Sanjo shopping street), Osaka Grand Front and the Kobe Kitano Starbucks cafe, then fly home from Kansai.
why: It is the only way to see the Sabbat places; Kansai also has Uji (Euphonium) and Toyosato (K-On) close by, and Kansai Airport has many flights to Shanghai.
duration: 3 days (replaces Furano→Sapporo, Sapporo day, and changes end city to Osaka)
cost: Flight Hokkaido→Osaka approx 12,000–25,000 JPY; local trains approx 3,000 JPY; hotels as normal
winterNote: All city spots, no snow problems. Kyoto Concert Hall is a working concert hall: outside photos only. Kobe Starbucks was renovated, so the inside differs from the game CG. Pegasis's Narita flight would change to a Kansai departure.

places.ja: 京都コンサートホール

places.en: Starbucks Kobe Kitano Ijinkan (cafe Schwarze Katze)
places.ja: スターバックスコーヒー 神戸北野異人館店

anime: Sabbat of the Witch (サノバウィッチ): school, station meetings, ramen shop, date mall, cafe Schwarze Katze. Also Inuzuka Bridge (犬塚橋) and Takaragaike-dori in north Kyoto.

experience.hook: Walk into Sabbat of the Witch's real Kyoto, Osaka and Kobe backgrounds.
moments: Stand at Kyoto Station's big hall, the crowded meeting place from the game, and match the CG angle.
Photograph Kyoto Concert Hall from outside, the stylish building used as the school.
Walk the covered Sanjo shopping arcade, where the heroine takes on the giant ramen challenge.
Stroll Grand Front Osaka at night, the mall of the date scenes, when it is quiet for photos.
Drink coffee in Starbucks Kobe Kitano Ijinkan, a 1907 Western house used as the game's cafe.
experience.tip: Save the game CGs on your phone before you go. Grand Front is quiet in the evening, good for matching shots.

title: Aokana pilgrimage, Goto Islands
titleJa: 蒼の彼方のフォーリズム 聖地巡礼（五島列島）
summary: Verified: the Four Islands of Aokana are modelled on the Goto Islands, Nagasaki (Fukue, Hisaka, Wakamatsu, Nakadori, Naru). Fly Hokkaido→Fukuoka, then a 40-min flight to Goto Fukue; rent a car for Takahama Beach (Flying Circus practice), Osezaki Lighthouse (date scene), Fukue samurai street (Misaki's house) and the Fukue arcade, then fly home from Fukuoka.
why: The main anime wish that no other part of the trip covers; the island coast is also very beautiful and quiet in winter.
duration: 3 days (2 nights Fukuoka/Goto); 4 days to add Naru Island and Hisaka Island by ferry
cost: New Chitose→Fukuoka approx 15,000–30,000 JPY; Fukuoka↔Goto Fukue (ANA/ORC) approx 15,000–25,000 JPY each way; rental car approx 6,000 JPY/day (all approx, not checked)
winterNote: No snow, but strong winter wind can cancel jetfoils and small planes; keep a spare half day. No direct Tokyo flight: go via Fukuoka (40 min, ANA/ORC) or Nagasaki (30 min), or jetfoil Nagasaki→Fukue 1 h 25–45 min. In 2026 an Aokana 10th-anniversary event (art show + digital stamp rally at 5 Goto spots) ran Jan 8–Mar 22; 2027 events not yet known. Osezaki Lighthouse needs about 20 min walk from the car park.

places.en: Fukue town: samurai street and arcade
places.ja: 福江武家屋敷通り・福江商店街アーケード

anime: Aokana: Four Rhythm Across the Blue (蒼の彼方のフォーリズム): Flying Circus practice beach, Misaki's house, lighthouse date. Other islands: Miyanohama Beach (Naru), Hamawaki Church (Hisaka), Naraō port (Kamigoto).

experience.hook: Fly to the real Four Islands where Aokana's kids race in the sky.
moments: Walk the roofed Fukue arcade, where the characters buy their Flying Circus shoes.
See Misaki's house gate on the Fukue samurai street, with an anime display and cast signatures.
Stand on white Takahama Beach, the Flying Circus practice and match place, in clear blue winter water.
Hike 20 minutes to Osezaki Lighthouse, the sunset date spot, above tall sea cliffs.
Eat hot Goto udon, pulled straight from a boiling pot and dipped in fish broth.
experience.tip: Get the Misaki goods and stamp at the samurai street hall. Keep a spare half day: winter wind stops jetfoils and small planes.

title: Sabbat plus Aokana west ending
titleJa: 関西・五島 聖地巡礼ルート
summary: One route that does both big wishes: shorten Hokkaido, fly Sapporo→Osaka, one day Kyoto/Uji, one day Osaka/Kobe, Shinkansen Shin-Kobe→Hakata (about 2 h 15), fly to Goto Fukue, then home from Fukuoka. This drops Asahikawa, Biei and Furano.
why: Covers Sabbat of the Witch and Aokana inside Aoki's 15-day limit.
cost: Flight Sapporo→Osaka approx 12,000–25,000 JPY; Shinkansen Shin-Kobe→Hakata approx 15,000 JPY; Fukuoka↔Goto approx 15,000–25,000 JPY each way (approx)
winterNote: Goto flights/jetfoils can stop in strong wind; put Goto before the last day, not on it. Loses the Asahiyama zoo and Blue Pond days.
anime: Sabbat of the Witch (Kyoto/Osaka/Kobe), Hibike! Euphonium (Uji), Aokana (Goto)

experience.hook: Three dream anime places in one trip: Kyoto, Uji and Goto.
moments: Photograph Kyoto Concert Hall, the Sabbat of the Witch school, then eat ramen in the Sanjo arcade.
Run across Uji Bridge like Kumiko in Euphonium, then climb Daikichiyama lookout for Reina's night view.
Drink coffee at Starbucks Kobe Kitano Ijinkan, the old Western house cafe from Sabbat of the Witch.
Ride the Shinkansen from Shin-Kobe to Hakata, then fly 40 minutes to Goto Fukue.
Stand on Takahama Beach and at Osezaki Lighthouse, Aokana's practice beach and sunset date spot.
experience.tip: Put Goto two days before your flight home. Wind can cancel island flights, and you need a spare day.

title: Kaguya-sama walk, Mita to Takeshiba
titleJa: かぐや様は告らせたい 聖地巡礼（三田・田町・新橋・竹芝）
summary: Kaguya-sama is set in Minato ward, Tokyo: the school walk is Mita-dori by Keio University, the shared-umbrella scene is Mita Kokusai Building, and the fireworks-night meeting point is Takeshiba Pier. Walk Tamachi → Mita → Shimbashi SL Plaza → Takeshiba (2–3 h), ideally at dusk for the bay view.
why: Easy Tokyo add-on on the JR Yamanote line, no extra travel day.
cost: approx 500 JPY trains
winterNote: City streets, open all year. The actual fireworks in the story are in Kisarazu (Chiba) in summer; in winter you only see the pier. Shinomiya house model (Tsunamachi Mitsui Club) is private: outside only.

places.ja: 三田通り・慶應義塾大学前

anime: Kaguya-sama: Love Is War (かぐや様は告らせたい) S1 ep 3, 5, 12 (fireworks); S2 Royal Host Takanawa and Tamachi

experience.hook: Walk Kaguya and Shirogane's school route, then end at the fireworks pier.
moments: Walk Mita-dori past Keio University, the school commute of Kaguya and Shirogane in season 1 ep 3.
Stand under Mita Kokusai Building, the street of the shared-umbrella scene in ep 5.
Find the black steam locomotive at Shimbashi SL Plaza, the volunteer scene in ep 5.
Pass Tokyo Ramen Tower in Shibadaimon, where Kaguya runs to the fireworks in ep 12.
Wait on Takeshiba Pier at dusk, the council's fireworks meeting place, with bay lights over the water.
experience.tip: Start at Tamachi around 14:00 so you reach Takeshiba Pier at sunset. In January the sun sets near 16:50.

title: Girls Band Cry: Yako and stamps
titleJa: ガールズバンドクライ 矢向・幸区・スタンプツアー
summary: Extra GBC places not in the plan: Yako Station and the Yako-yu bathhouse (Nina's area, ep 1–2), Saiwai green path, and Shinmei Shrine by Kawaracho estate (ep 12 'ROCK no Kamisama', ep 13). Collect the official 'Girls Band Cry Stamp Tour' stamps (stamp book sold at stamp spots) and, if time, FRO CAFE at Musashi-Kosugi.
why: Deepens the Kawasaki day with the quiet local spots fans love, and you can take a real sento bath where Nina did.
cost: Sento approx 550 JPY; stamp book approx 1,000–2,000 JPY (not checked); trains approx 500 JPY
winterNote: Yako-yu opens 15:00–22:00, irregular closing days. FRO CAFE 11:30–21:00, closed Mondays. Stamp tour has grown to 25+ spots (e.g. Kawasaki Aquarium and Kawasaki Daishi from Feb 27, 2026); check the list in Jan 2027. Some spots changed: Island Mura Guitars (Lazona) closed Sep 23, 2026. Frontale (Todoroki) has winter break in late Jan, no match.

places.ja: 河原町団地・神明町児童公園

anime: Girls Band Cry (ガールズバンドクライ) ep 1, 2, 9, 12, 13

experience.hook: Go deep into Nina's Kawasaki neighbourhood and collect Girls Band Cry stamps.
moments: Walk the Saiwai green path, Nina's route home in ep 1.
Soak in Yako-yu, the old bathhouse on Nina's street, with Girls Band Cry goods on show.
See Kawaracho estate, Rupa's home, with its big grey blocks and small shops below.
Stand at Shinmei Shrine at night, the place of the night performance in ep 12 and the choice in ep 13.
Stamp your Girls Band Cry stamp book at each shop, then eat lunch at FRO CAFE, Musashi-Kosugi.
experience.tip: Rent a bicycle: spots are far apart. Yako-yu opens at 15:00, so do it last and warm up after the cold ride.

title: Girls Band Cry Tokyo scenes
titleJa: ガールズバンドクライ 東京編（東京駅・渋谷・武道館）
summary: GBC also uses Tokyo: the Tokyo Station Marunouchi South dome (ep 1, Nina arrives), Shibuya Hachiko and Spain-zaka (ep 3), Cafe Renoir by Shibuya Hands (ep 4) and the Nippon Budokan (ep 6). Easy to fit between other Tokyo stops.
why: Fans of the show can add these with almost no extra travel time.
cost: approx 500 JPY trains
winterNote: Public places, open all year. Budokan is outside only unless there is a concert.

places.ja: 東京駅 丸の内南口ドーム

anime: Girls Band Cry ep 1, 3, 4, 6 (also Oimachi and Shinagawa stations, Shakujii Park)

experience.hook: Stand where Nina first steps into Tokyo in Girls Band Cry.
moments: Look up at the Tokyo Station Marunouchi dome, where Nina arrives in ep 1.
Stand by Hachiko in Shibuya and walk up narrow Spain-zaka stairs, both from ep 3.
Drink coffee in Cafe Renoir by Shibuya Hands, the talking scene of ep 4.
Walk to the Nippon Budokan gate, the big stage the band dreams about in ep 6.
experience.tip: Go to Spain-zaka before 10:00. The shops are shut and the stairs are empty, so your photo matches the anime frame.

title: More Bocchi spots in Shimokitazawa
titleJa: ぼっち・ざ・ろっく！ 下北沢 聖地（本多劇場・どんぐりひろば公園ほか）
summary: Beyond the station and SHELTER: Honda Theater ('Honmaru Gekijo' in the show), Donguri Hiroba park with spring-ride toys (ep 4), the Senrogai empty lot with the big pipe (ep 5), the 'Geki' small theater wall (ep 1) and the 'artist photo' ivy wall at Times Shimokitazawa 8. About half of the 50+ Bocchi spots are here.
why: Turns a quick stop into a full Bocchi walk in the same area on day 2.
cost: free
winterNote: The Times parking ivy wall is in a road-widening zone and may be gone; winter ivy has no leaves. Photos of SHELTER only on weekdays, small groups. Do not photograph private houses.

places.ja: 下北線路街 空き地

anime: Bocchi the Rock! (ぼっち・ざ・ろっく！) ep 1, 4, 5, 8

experience.hook: Find the small corners of Shimokitazawa where Bocchi hides and hopes.
moments: Walk past the 'Geki' small theater wall, seen in ep 1 on the way to STARRY.
Sit on the spring-ride animal toys in Donguri Hiroba park, the artist photo shoot of ep 4.
Find the tree mural and ivy wall at Times Shimokitazawa 8, the band's artist photo wall in ep 4.
Crouch by the big drain pipes in the Senrogai empty lot, where Bocchi sits sad in ep 5.
Look at SHELTER's door, the real live house behind STARRY.
experience.tip: Go on a weekday before 14:00: fewer people, and SHELTER asks for no weekend or evening photos. Keep your voice low.

title: Bocchi's home town, Kanazawa-hakkei
titleJa: ぼっち・ざ・ろっく！ 金沢八景（横浜市）
summary: Bocchi lives in the Kanazawa-hakkei area of Yokohama. See Kanazawa-hakkei Station and the Seaside Line overpass benches where Hitori and Kikuri play on the street (ep 6), Biwajima Shrine and the Hiragata Bay promenade.
why: Quiet, few tourists, and on the same Keikyu line as Kawasaki (about 30 min), so it fits the Kawasaki day.
cost: approx 800 JPY trains
winterNote: Outdoor seaside spots, open all year; short winter daylight, go in the morning.
anime: Bocchi the Rock! ep 6 (street live with Kikuri), Bocchi's home area

experience.hook: Visit Bocchi's home town, where she plays her first street live.
moments: Step out at Kanazawa-hakkei Station, the start of Bocchi's long commute to Shimokitazawa.
Stand under the Seaside Line tracks, where Bocchi and Kikuri play the street live in ep 6.
Walk the Hiragata Bay promenade by the water, Bocchi's daily route in the anime backgrounds.
Cross the red bridge to little Biwajima Shrine, where Kikuri meets Bocchi.
experience.tip: Go in the morning. Winter sun is low and soft, and the promenade is quiet for matching shots.

title: Enoshima and Slam Dunk crossing
titleJa: 江の島・鎌倉高校前踏切
summary: Ride the Enoden to the Kamakura-Koko-mae rail crossing from the Slam Dunk opening, then walk to Enoshima for Bocchi episode 9 (Katase-Enoshima station, Asahi tako-senbei, Enoshima Shrine red torii). Clear winter days often show Mt Fuji across the bay at sunset.
why: Two famous anime spots plus sea and Fuji views in one easy day from Tokyo.
cost: approx 2,000 JPY trains
winterNote: Open all year; winter has clearer air for Fuji. The crossing is very busy and has guards; stay on the sidewalk and do not stand in the road.

places.ja: 鎌倉高校前駅 踏切

anime: Slam Dunk opening; Bocchi the Rock! ep 9 'Enoshima Escar'

experience.hook: See the Slam Dunk crossing, then climb Enoshima like the Bocchi band.
moments: Watch a green Enoden train pass the Kamakura-Koko-mae crossing, blue sea behind: the Slam Dunk opening shot.
Walk out of Katase-Enoshima Station, the red dragon-palace station from Bocchi ep 9.
Eat a hot tako-senbei at Asahi Honten, a whole octopus pressed flat, like the band in ep 9.
Climb to the red torii and stone steps of Enoshima Shrine, or ride the Escar like tired Bocchi.
Watch Mt Fuji go dark orange across the bay from the island's west side at sunset.
experience.tip: Trains pass the crossing about every 12 minutes. Stand on the sidewalk, not the road, and follow the guards.

title: Numazu, Love Live! Sunshine!!
titleJa: ラブライブ！サンシャイン!! 沼津・内浦
summary: On the way back from Fuji, go to Numazu instead of straight to Tokyo: Uchiura bay with Yasudaya Ryokan (Chika's house model), Awashima island and Izu-Mito Sea Paradise, then Numazu town with Aqours manholes and shops. Return by Shinkansen from Mishima.
why: One of the biggest pilgrimage towns in Japan (Anime Tourism 88), and the sea with Fuji behind it fits the Fuji days.
duration: 1 day (replaces the afternoon in Tokyo / Shibuya Sky)
cost: approx 5,000–8,000 JPY (bus/train + Shinkansen Mishima→Tokyo)
winterNote: Mild coast, no snow. Awashima island cafe/boat has its own opening days; check before going.

places.ja: 伊豆・三津シーパラダイス

anime: Love Live! Sunshine!! (Aqours, Uranohoshi)

experience.hook: Walk Aqours' seaside home town, with Mt Fuji over Uchiura bay.
moments: Find the nine Aqours manhole covers around Numazu Station, one for each girl.
Ride the bus to Uchiura and stand in front of Yasudaya Ryokan, Chika's family inn.
Take the Aqours-wrapped boat to Awashima; see the Frog Museum, Kanan's diving shop model.
Visit Izu-Mito Sea Paradise, home of the mascot Uchicchi, and watch the sea lions.
Eat fresh horse mackerel or shirasu bowls at Numazu Port, then see the Deep Sea Aquarium coelacanth.
experience.tip: Go on a clear morning for Fuji over the bay. Awashima boats run 10:00–16:20 in winter and stop in bad weather.

title: Yuru Camp Motosu lake view
titleJa: ゆるキャン△ 浩庵キャンプ場（本栖湖）
summary: Koan Campsite on Lake Motosu is where Rin camps in Yuru Camp episode 1 and Nadeshiko sees Fuji; it is also the Fuji view on the 1,000-yen note. About 25 min by car west of Kawaguchiko.
why: Yuru Camp is a winter-camping anime, so late January is the exact season of the show, and you already have a car on day 4.
cost: free (parking small fee may apply)
winterNote: Very cold at dawn; roads can be icy, winter tyres needed. Best Fuji view in the morning.
anime: Yuru Camp△ (ゆるキャン△) episode 1

experience.hook: Stand where Rin camps and Nadeshiko sees Fuji in Yuru Camp episode 1.
moments: Walk down to the Koan Campsite shore, Rin's quiet solo camp in episode 1.
See the toilet building bench where Nadeshiko falls asleep after her long bike ride.
Hold an old 1,000-yen note up to Fuji over Lake Motosu, the same view as the note.
Eat curry cup noodles on the shore in the cold, like Rin and Nadeshiko.
experience.tip: Arrive just after sunrise: the lake is calm, so Fuji shows upside-down in the water. Bring gloves; it is often below zero.

title: Hakodate: Saint Snow and Conan
titleJa: 函館 聖地巡礼（ラブライブ！サンシャイン!!・名探偵コナン）
summary: Hakodate is an Anime Tourism 88 spot for Love Live! Sunshine!! S2 ep 8–9 (Saint Snow's family cafe model Sabo Kikuizumi, Kanemori red brick warehouses, Mt Hakodate night view). The 2024 Conan movie 'The Million-dollar Pentagram' uses Goryokaku, and Golden Kamuy uses the Benten Daiba fort site.
why: Already on the route; the snowy night view is also how the Aqours episode looks.
cost: approx 1,500–3,000 JPY (ropeway, tram, Goryokaku Tower)
winterNote: Snowy slopes in Motomachi; wear shoes with grip. Mt Hakodate ropeway runs in winter but can stop in strong wind.

places.ja: 五稜郭跡 箱館奉行所

anime: Love Live! Sunshine!! S2 ep 8–9; Detective Conan movie 2024; Golden Kamuy
photoQuery: Kanemori Red Brick Warehouse Hakodate snow

experience.hook: Walk snowy Hakodate, home of Saint Snow and Conan's star fort.
moments: Visit Sabo Kikuizumi, the old house cafe that models the Saint Snow sisters' family home.
Walk down the snowy Hachimanzaka slope, the bay and harbour straight ahead, like Aqours in S2.
Walk the Kanemori red brick warehouses by the water, part of the Hakodate episodes.
See Goryokaku's star-shaped moat from the tower, the fort of the 2024 Conan movie.
Ride the ropeway up Mt Hakodate for the city lights between two dark bays.
experience.tip: Go to Goryokaku after dark: the Star Dream lights trace the star shape in winter. Wear shoes with grip on the slopes.

title: Otaru anime and Golden Kamuy
titleJa: 小樽 聖地巡礼（ゴールデンカムイ・最終兵器彼女）
summary: Otaru appears in Golden Kamuy (Taisho Glass main shop), Saikano (Otaru Canal, Asahi lookout, aquarium) and Hidamari Sketch x Honeycomb (canal, former NYK building, music box museum). A short walk while you pass Otaru.
why: Small bonus on a day already in Otaru; the snowy canal is a classic winter photo.
cost: free
winterNote: Otaru Snow Light Path festival is usually in early/mid February, so likely after your visit; check 2027 dates.
anime: Golden Kamuy; Saikano; Hidamari Sketch x Honeycomb

experience.hook: See Otaru's snowy canal and glass shops from Golden Kamuy and Saikano.
moments: Walk into Otaru Taisho Glass main shop, a stone building from a Golden Kamuy scene.
Walk the snowy Otaru Canal, seen in every Saikano episode and the Hidamari school trip.
Listen to the steam clock whistle outside the Otaru Music Box Museum, a Hidamari Sketch stop.
Climb to Asahi lookout, Chise and Shuji's hill in Saikano, for the view over the port.
experience.tip: Get to the canal at dusk: the gas lamps come on and the snow turns blue. The best photo is from Asakusa Bridge.

title: Ghibli Museum, Mitaka
titleJa: 三鷹の森ジブリ美術館
summary: Studio Ghibli's own museum with a short film only shown there. Timed tickets only, sold online; 15 min by train from Shinjuku plus a walk along the Tamagawa aqueduct.
why: Must-see for anime fans, and it is close to the Shinjuku hotel.
cost: 1,000 JPY adult
winterNote: Tickets for January go on sale Dec 10, 2026, 10:00 JST (Lawson Ticket, overseas site) and sell out fast. Usually closed Tuesdays (Jan 19, Jan 26, Feb 2) and in some maintenance periods; check the Jan 2027 calendar.
anime: Studio Ghibli (Totoro, Spirited Away, etc.)

experience.hook: Enter Miyazaki's own museum and see a short film shown nowhere else.
moments: Walk along the Tamagawa aqueduct from Mitaka Station, past the Totoro at the fake ticket booth.
Get your ticket: a strip of real 35 mm film from a Ghibli movie.
Watch the Ghibli short film in the small Saturn Theater, shown only here.
Climb the spiral iron stairs to the roof and stand by the 5 m Laputa robot soldier.
Eat in the Straw Hat Cafe, then shop at Mamma Aiuto.
experience.tip: Buy tickets Dec 10 at 10:00 JST, the moment they go on sale. Photos are not allowed inside, so take them on the roof.

title: Chichibu: Anohana and icicles
titleJa: 秩父 聖地巡礼（あの花・ここさけ・空の青さを知る人よ）
summary: Chichibu is the town of Anohana, Kokosake and Her Blue Sky (all Anime Tourism 88). See the old Chichibu Bridge from the Anohana ending, Chichibu Shrine and the station area, 80 min from Ikebukuro by Seibu Laview.
why: The classic tear-jerker pilgrimage, and in winter the Misotsuchi icicles nearby are a big bonus.
cost: approx 3,000–4,000 JPY trains
winterNote: Misotsuchi icicles (三十槌の氷柱) usually show mid-Jan to late Feb with some evening light-ups; check 2027 dates. Cold, but little snow in town.
anime: Anohana (あの日見た花の名前を僕達はまだ知らない。), Kokosake, Her Blue Sky

experience.hook: Cross the bridge from the Anohana ending, then see blue winter icicles.
moments: Walk the old Chichibu Bridge, the arch bridge from the Anohana ending and posters.
Visit Teirinji, temple 17 of the Chichibu pilgrimage, whose sign shows in ep 4.
See Chichibu Shrine's carved gate and stone entrance, also in ep 4.
Eat a waraji katsu-don, two big sandal-shaped pork cutlets on rice, a Chichibu dish.
See the Misotsuchi icicles, a white wall of ice by the river, lit up some evenings.
experience.tip: Go to the icicles after dark if a light-up runs: the ice glows blue and white. Check the 2027 dates first.

title: Washinomiya Shrine, Lucky Star
titleJa: らき☆すた 鷲宮神社
summary: The shrine of the Hiiragi sisters in Lucky Star, the place that started modern anime pilgrimage in Japan. Buy an ita-ema, see the fan boards; about 1 h from Tokyo by Tobu line.
why: Historic spot for anime fans, short trip.
cost: approx 1,500 JPY trains
winterNote: New Year crowds are over by late January; open all year.
anime: Lucky Star (らき☆すた)

experience.hook: Visit the shrine from the Lucky Star opening, where anime pilgrimage began.
moments: Walk under the big wooden torii from the Lucky Star opening, the Hiiragi sisters' shrine.
Read the fan ema boards covered in anime drawings and messages, like the ones in ep 21.
Buy an ema and draw your own character on it.
Eat at Ootori Chaya, the old-style tea house on the shrine approach.
experience.tip: Draw your ema at home first with a fine black pen. Fans take pride in good ema drawings.

title: Oarai, Girls und Panzer
titleJa: ガールズ&パンツァー 大洗
summary: Oarai town is covered with Girls und Panzer panels and shop tie-ins; see the Kamiiso torii on the rocks at Oarai Isosaki Shrine and the Marine Tower area. About 2 h from Tokyo via Mito.
why: One of the friendliest anime towns in Japan (Anime Tourism 88), plus winter monkfish (anko) hot pot.
cost: approx 5,000–8,000 JPY trains
winterNote: Winter is anko season. Windy on the coast. Kamiiso torii sunrise is a famous photo.

places.ja: 大洗磯前神社・神磯の鳥居

anime: Girls und Panzer (ガールズ&パンツァー) incl. Das Finale

experience.hook: Visit the seaside town where tanks crash through real shops in Girls und Panzer.
moments: Walk the shopping streets from Oarai Station, with life-size Girls und Panzer panels at shop doors.
See Sakanaya Honten inn, hit by a tank in the St. Gloriana practice match.
Visit Garupan Gallery in Oarai Marine Tower, then look over the town from the 60 m deck.
Stand by the Kamiiso torii on sea rocks at Oarai Isosaki Shrine as waves hit.
Eat anko-nabe, rich monkfish hot pot, the local winter dish.
experience.tip: Go at sunrise for the Kamiiso torii: the sun behind the torii is the famous shot. Winter has the clearest air.

title: Hida: Your Name and Hyouka
titleJa: 飛騨古川・高山（君の名は。・氷菓）
summary: Hida-Furukawa Station and Keta Wakamiya Shrine are Your Name scenes; Takayama old town and Nakabashi bridge are Hyouka's Kamiyama city. Deep snow in January makes it a winter postcard.
why: Two big titles in one snowy old town, a different winter scene from Zao.
cost: approx 15,000–20,000 JPY trains (Tokyo→Toyama Shinkansen + Takayama line) plus ryokan
winterNote: Snow and cold; Takayama line can delay in heavy snow. No ski resort for Pegasis unless you add one. Returning north to Hokkaido needs a long day via Tokyo.
anime: Your Name (君の名は。); Hyouka (氷菓)

experience.hook: Walk the snowy towns of Your Name and Hyouka.
moments: Stand at Hida-Furukawa Station, where Taki gets off to look for Mitsuha's town.
Visit Hida City Library, where Taki and his friends search the records of Itomori.
Walk the snowy white-wall storehouses along the Setogawa canal in Furukawa.
Stand on red Nakabashi bridge in Takayama, the heart of Hyouka's Kamiyama city.
Eat Hida beef sushi on a rice cracker in Sanmachi old street.
experience.tip: Ask at the library counter before you take photos inside. Take the Takayama line early: heavy snow can delay trains.

title: Uji Euphonium and Toyosato K-On
titleJa: 宇治（響け！ユーフォニアム）・豊郷小学校旧校舎群（けいおん！）
summary: Only with a Kansai ending: Uji Bridge and Daikichiyama lookout from Hibike! Euphonium (30 min from Kyoto), and the old Toyosato school, the K-On school model with the tea-time club room (1 h from Kyoto).
why: Adds two much-loved Kyoto Animation settings to the Sabbat Kansai days.
cost: approx 1,000–3,000 JPY trains
winterNote: Daikichiyama is a short hill hike, can be icy. Toyosato old school is open to visitors on most days; check closed days.
anime: Hibike! Euphonium (響け！ユーフォニアム); K-On! (けいおん！)

experience.hook: Run Kumiko's bridge in Uji, then drink tea in the K-On club room.
moments: Run across Uji Bridge like Kumiko in season 1 ep 12, shouting she wants to get better.
Climb Daikichiyama to the lookout where Kumiko and Reina play together in season 1 ep 8.
Drink matcha at Tsuen, the old tea shop at the end of Uji Bridge.
Touch the rabbit and tortoise statues on the Toyosato school stair rail, seen in K-On.
Sit in the recreated K-On club room, with tea set and instruments laid out by fans.
experience.tip: Toyosato old school is closed on Mondays. Climb Daikichiyama around sunset for the Uji city lights, and bring a torch.

title: Hakone as Evangelion Tokyo-3
titleJa: 箱根（エヴァンゲリオン 第3新東京市）
summary: Evangelion's Tokyo-3 is set in Hakone (Sengokuhara and Lake Ashi area). Look for Eva tie-ins around Hakone-Yumoto and Owakudani on the drive day.
why: Small anime bonus on a day already in Hakone.
cost: free
winterNote: Eva shops and collab items change often; not checked for 2027. Owakudani can close due to volcanic gas.
anime: Neon Genesis Evangelion (Tokyo-3)

experience.hook: Drive through Hakone, the real ground under Evangelion's Tokyo-3.
moments: Drive through Sengokuhara, the center of Tokyo-3, with Mt Kintoki above the valley.
Stand on the north shore of Lake Ashi, where the city meets the water in the anime.
Eat a black egg at Owakudani, boiled in the hot volcanic spring, with steam around you.
Look for Eva goods in shops around Hakone-Yumoto Station, the start of the drive.
experience.tip: Play the Eva opening song as you drive into Sengokuhara. Check Owakudani's status online first: volcanic gas can close it.

title: Rusutsu snow drift driving course
titleJa: ルスツリゾート 雪上ドリフト
summary: A closed snow course at Rusutsu Resort, about 40 min from Niseko, with Subaru, GT-R and GR Yaris cars. You can ride with a pro rally driver (4 min) or drive yourself with an instructor next to you (30 or 75 min).
why: The only real 'you drive, you drift' option on the route that does not need a 3-year licence: Pegasis can drive on private ground, and Aoki can ride along or drive too.
cost: Ride-along Subaru B4 ¥17,000 (1–2 people), GT-R or GR Yaris ride ¥27,000; drive yourself: intro 30 min ¥31,000, full course 75 min ¥61,000; rear-seat rider ¥10,000–20,000
winterNote: Season mid-Dec 2026 to late Feb 2027. Slots 8:30, 10:00, 13:00, 15:00. Book by 17:00 the day before. Driving needs a valid licence (bring IDP); instructor can refuse you if unsafe. No minimum years stated, but ask by email first.

experience.hook: Slide a 4WD Subaru sideways across a snowed-in golf course.
moments: Check in at the Rusutsu Resort Hotel Activity Desk, blow into the breathalyzer, then ride the shuttle 15 minutes to the course.
Step out onto the Riverwood golf course, now a white track of packed snow and snow banks.
Hold on in a GT-R or GR Yaris while the instructor throws it sideways, snow spraying past the window.
Drive a Subaru B4 or automatic Impreza yourself, and feel the rear step out as the instructor calls the steering.
Film the ride from the passenger seat; filming is allowed, so bring a phone mount or chest strap.
experience.tip: Book by 17:00 the day before. Take the 8:30 slot for fresh, even snow. Wear warm shoes you can feel pedals in; rental shoes exist.

title: Initial D Mt Haruna day trip
titleJa: 頭文字D 聖地 榛名山（秋名山）
summary: Drive from Tokyo to Gunma and run the real 'Akina' downhill (Prefectural Route 33) past the Yaseone old toll gate and the five hairpins to Lake Haruna. Stop at Ikaho Onsen stone steps and the Ikaho toy and car museum, which shows a Fujiwara Tofu Shop display.
why: It is the number one JDM pilgrimage site, and it mixes the anime and car interests with an onsen town.
duration: 1 day (about 2–2.5 h each way from Tokyo by car)
cost: Rental car ~¥10,000–15,000/day shared + fuel/tolls; museum fee: check
winterNote: Road is open in winter, but it is at high altitude with snow and ice risk Dec–Mar. Studless tyres are a must; both can drive a normal rental car; Aoki takes the icy parts. Go only on a clear day. Add Usui pass (Route 18, Megane Bridge) if time allows.

places.en: Yaseone pass old toll gate (race start)
places.ja: ヤセオネ峠 旧料金所

places.en: Ikaho Toy, Doll and Car Museum (tofu shop display)
places.ja: 伊香保おもちゃと人形 自動車博物館
碓氷第三橋梁（めがね橋）

anime: Initial D — Akina downhill battles (Takumi's tofu delivery route)

experience.hook: Drive Takumi's real tofu run down 'Akina' to Lake Haruna.
moments: Stand at the Yaseone old toll gate by the water tower, the start line of the Akina downhill races.
Drive the tight hairpins slowly and look at the gutters, where Takumi does his famous gutter-drop move.
Walk to frozen-edged Lake Haruna and see the Mt Haruna cone reflected across the water.
Look at the Fujiwara Tofu Shop storefront and AE86 displays in the Ikaho car museum.
Climb the 365 Ikaho stone steps and eat hot yu-no-hana manju, the same buns from the anime.
experience.tip: Go on a clear, dry day and drive the pass before noon, before shade ice forms. The road surface is rough, so go slow.

title: Irohazaka hairpins and Nikko
titleJa: いろは坂（日光）
summary: Irohazaka is two one-way mountain roads with 48 hairpins (20 up, 28 down) to Lake Chuzenji. You can ride it on the normal local bus from Nikko station, then see Toshogu shrine and the Akechidaira view.
why: It is the home road of team Emperor in Initial D Third Stage, and nobody needs to drive, so Pegasis's licence does not matter.
cost: approx ¥6,000–9,000 return train (Tobu line) + local bus; check current fares
winterNote: Road is open all year (free road since 1984), but snow and ice are common in late Jan; buses still run. Some upper sights may be closed in winter. Self-drive only with studless tyres (Aoki).
anime: Initial D Third Stage — team Emperor at Irohazaka

experience.hook: Ride a normal city bus up 48 hairpins, each one marked with a letter.
moments: Sit at the front of the bus from Nikko station and count the hiragana signs: い, ろ, は, one per hairpin.
Climb 440 m on the uphill Second Irohazaka, the road where team Emperor's Evos race in Initial D Third Stage.
Stand at Kegon Falls, a 97 m drop that is often partly frozen into ice columns in January.
Walk the snowy approach to Toshogu shrine and find the carved Sleeping Cat and three wise monkeys.
Ride back down the separate one-way First Irohazaka, with its 28 downhill curves.
experience.tip: Sit on the left front seat going up for the best hairpin view. Check if the Akechidaira ropeway runs in winter before you plan it.

title: Frozen lake ice driving, Nagano
titleJa: 女神湖 氷上ドライブ
summary: Lake Megami (1,540 m) freezes in winter and becomes an ice course where cars slide from 20 km/h. Clubs and driving coaches run full-day ice lessons with lunch.
why: Ice car control on private ground is the dream JDM winter skill, and Pegasis can drive there.
cost: Per car per day ¥30,000–53,000 (lunch included), passenger +¥2,500
winterNote: 2026 dates were e.g. Jan 19–20, Jan 31–Feb 2, Feb 6–7; 2027 dates not yet out. Most events need YOUR OWN car (studless, under 2.5 t), so it is hard for tourists. Fun2Drive (Hakone rental) ran a rental-car ice event at Yachiho Lake in 2026: ask them for 2027.

experience.hook: Learn to steer with the throttle on a frozen lake 1,540 m up.
moments: Arrive at 07:00 as the gate opens, with the lake white and flat, and the cold biting through your gloves.
Weave a pylon slalom in the orange area, feeling the car start to slide at just 20 km/h.
Hold a steady circle and figure eight in the green area until the slide feels natural.
Warm up with the included lunch and free drinks around 11:00.
Run the 500 m ice circuit in the blue area and link the corners in long slides.
experience.tip: Most events need your own car on studless tyres. Ask Fun2Drive in Hakone early if their rental-car ice event runs again in 2027.

title: Ebisu Circuit drift taxi (closed)
titleJa: エビスサーキット ドリフトタクシー
summary: Famous drift passenger ride in Fukushima, near the Tohoku Shinkansen route. A pro drifts you around the circuit with up to 3 riders per car.
why: Would be the perfect Tohoku stop, but it does not run in the trip dates.
cost: ¥45,000 per car (max 3 people) + ¥500 insurance each
winterNote: Closed in winter: Dec 20 – Mar 31 (snow). Official page also showed 'temporarily closed' in 2026. Do not plan it for Jan 2027.

experience.hook: A D1 champion drifts you around Ebisu in a Mark II taxi.
moments: Buckle into the bucket seats of the drift taxi, a Toyota Mark II JZX110.
Ride with Nobushige Kumakubo, D1GP champion in 2006 and 2011, or KANTA, 2023 Formula Drift Japan champion.
Hear the tyres scream and smell the rubber smoke as the car links corners at full lock.
Watch practice cars on the other Ebisu courses from the hillside after your ride.
experience.tip: Not possible on this trip: closed Dec 20 to Mar 31, and paused since 2025. Keep it for a spring or autumn visit.

title: Guided circuit drift day from Tokyo
titleJa: ドリフト体験ツアー（東京発）
summary: Tour companies pick you up in central Tokyo and take you to a circuit to drive or ride in a real drift car, with instructor and lunch. About 6 h of track time.
why: A full drift day for JDM fans; Aoki can drive and Pegasis can ride if too young or too new to drive.
cost: ¥75,000–205,000 depending on car; ¥100,000 refundable deposit
winterNote: Driver must be 26+ with IDP; passengers any age. Which circuit is used in winter is not stated (Ebisu is closed in winter) — ask the operator before booking.

experience.hook: Pick your JDM hero car, from R34 to Nismo GT-R, and drift it.
moments: Get picked up at your hotel at 07:00 and listen to the safety briefing on the drive out.
Choose your car: R34 Skyline, Supra MK4, RX-7 FD, Integra Type R, WRX STI S202, or an R35 GT-R.
Drive three hours of drift sessions from 09:00 with an instructor beside you, first slow circles, then linked slides.
Eat the included lunch at 12:00, then do two more hours of sessions in the afternoon.
Ride passenger with the instructor to feel a full-speed drift before you head back.
experience.tip: Only drivers aged 26+ with an IDP can drive. Ask which circuit they use in January before paying the ¥100,000 deposit.

title: Fuji Motorsports Museum and Speedway
titleJa: 富士モータースポーツミュージアム
summary: Museum at the gate of Fuji Speedway with about 100 years of race cars from Toyota, Nissan, Honda and others. You can also look at the circuit and Mt Fuji behind it.
why: It sits between Hakone and Kawaguchiko on day 4, so it is an easy stop for race-car fans.
cost: Adult ¥1,800 weekday at the window (¥1,600 online)
winterNote: Open daily 10:00–17:00, no regular closed day. Online booking opens the month before and gets priority.

experience.hook: See the Le Mans-winning Mazda 787B next to Fuji Speedway.
moments: Start with the oldest cars: an 1899 Panhard et Levassor and the 1902 Ford 999.
Stand in front of the 1965 Honda RA272, the first Japanese car to win an F1 race.
Look at the orange and green 1991 Mazda 787B, the first Japanese Le Mans overall winner.
Find the rally cars: Subaru Impreza 555 and Mitsubishi Lancer 1600GSR, then the HKS GR Supra drift car.
Step outside to see the long Fuji Speedway straight with snowy Mt Fuji behind it.
experience.tip: Book online a month ahead for ¥1,600. Exhibits rotate, so check the site's exhibit list before you go.

title: Nissan Heritage Collection, Zama
titleJa: 日産ヘリテージコレクション（座間）
summary: A garage in Nissan's Zama plant holding about 400 historic cars: Skyline GT-Rs, race cars, Z cars. Timed guided visits of about 80 minutes; on weekdays they sometimes start engines.
why: The best GT-R and Skyline collection in the world, free, one hour from Shinjuku.
cost: Free (reservation required)
winterNote: Weekdays only (Mon–Fri, about 10:00–16:00); Jan 19–22 are weekdays. Apply online in Japanese and wait for approval; slots fill fast, so apply about 1 month ahead.

experience.hook: Walk rows of 300 Nissans, and hear some of them start.
moments: Walk into the long hall inside Nissan's Zama plant with about 300 cars in rows.
Find the 1969 'Hakosuka' Skyline GT-R and the S30 Fairlady Z from the same year.
See the Group A Skyline race cars and the R390 GT1 Le Mans car.
Listen as the guide starts the engines of some cars on weekdays; about 70% still run.
Look back at 1930s Datsuns and 1950s–60s Prince Skylines to see where the GT-R started.
experience.tip: Apply online about a month ahead and pick a weekday slot, because weekday tours sometimes include engine starts. Entry is free.

title: Tatsumi PA and Umihotaru night
titleJa: 辰巳第一PA・海ほたるPA
summary: Add Tatsumi PA (small car meet spot with a city skyline view) and Umihotaru (rest stop island in Tokyo Bay) to the Daikoku PA night. You reach them only by car on the expressway.
why: More night car-meet spots on the same drive as Daikoku, with Aoki at the wheel or with a guided JDM night tour.
cost: Free entry; expressway tolls (Aqualine to Umihotaru) or a guided night tour (price varies by company)
winterNote: Meets are best on Friday/Saturday nights; Jan 21, 2027 is a Thursday, so fewer cars. Police sometimes close PAs at night when crowded.

experience.hook: Sit in a JDM meet under the city lights, then drive under the sea.
moments: Pull into Tatsumi PA, a small parking area on the expressway with the city skyline right behind the parked cars.
Walk the rows and look for tuned Skylines, Silvias and RX-7s, but do not touch the cars.
Drive into the 9.6 km Aqualine tunnel that runs under Tokyo Bay.
Come up at Umihotaru, a rest stop island in the bay, and walk the open deck in the cold sea wind.
See the lights of the bay, and on clear nights Mt Fuji in the distance.
experience.tip: Friday or Saturday nights get the most cars. The Aqualine toll is about ¥3,140 by cash. Police may close Tatsumi when it gets busy.

title: Nissan Crossing Ginza showroom
titleJa: NISSAN CROSSING（ニッサン クロッシング）
summary: Nissan's free showroom at the main Ginza crossing, with new and special cars and a café. Easy 30-minute stop in central Tokyo.
why: Quick free car stop in the city on the anime day.
cost: Free (café extra)
winterNote: Open all year; check the site for cars on display in Jan 2027.

experience.hook: Free Nissan showroom on the most famous corner in Ginza.
moments: Walk into Ginza Place at the Ginza 4-chome crossing and see the display cars under bright white lights.
Look at the new and special Nissan models, which change during the year.
Go up to the café and order a drink while you look down at the Ginza crossing.
Buy Nissan and GT-R goods in the shop before you leave.
experience.tip: Go after dark, when the Wako clock tower and Ginza lights are on outside. Check the site for the cars on show in January.

title: Honda Collection Hall, Motegi
titleJa: ホンダコレクションホール（モビリティリゾートもてぎ）
summary: Honda's own museum inside the Motegi circuit, with F1 cars, NSX, Type R and motorbikes. Entry is included in the resort ticket.
why: Honda heritage in one hall; can pair with Nikko/Irohazaka as a north Kanto car day.
duration: half day + 2.5 h travel each way
cost: No extra museum fee; pay resort entrance + parking only (check fee)
winterNote: Check the Motegi opening calendar for late Jan 2027. Hard without a car (bus from Utsunomiya is limited).

experience.hook: Honda keeps about 350 machines here, and all of them still run.
moments: Start at the Honda Dream A from 1947, the first product with the Honda name.
See the T360 mini truck from 1963, Honda's first four-wheeler.
Stand at the white and red RA272, Honda's first F1 winner in 1965.
Look at the NR500 race bike with its strange oval pistons.
Watch a scheduled engine start-up demo, then meet the ASIMO robots.
experience.tip: Check the Motegi calendar first: the hall has winter closure days. Use the free smartphone audio guide and bring earphones.

title: Start trip at Tokyo Auto Salon
titleJa: 東京オートサロン2027
summary: The biggest tuning car show in Asia, at Makuhari Messe near Narita, Jan 15–17, 2027. Arrive Jan 14–15, spend Saturday at the show, then run the same route 4–5 days earlier.
why: Every JDM tuner, demo car and drift star in one place — the peak event for their interests.
duration: 1 day at show; whole trip shifts ~4 days earlier
cost: Ticket ¥3,000 Sat/Sun (09:00–19:00 / 18:00), ¥4,000 Fri (public from 14:00); digital advance tickets only
winterNote: Aoki's 15-day visa limit means an earlier end: about Jan 15 – Jan 29. Flights are not booked yet, so this is possible. Weekend is very crowded; go at opening.

experience.hook: Asia's biggest tuning show fills eleven halls near Narita.
moments: Get to Makuhari Messe before 09:00 and go straight to the booths with new car reveals.
Walk Halls 1 to 11 past widebody builds, tuned GT-Rs and Supras, and maker booths like GR and NISMO.
Go outside to the demo area and watch drift runs, with engine noise and tyre smoke in the cold air.
Look for pro drivers signing autographs at the maker booths.
Buy tuner stickers, keychains and shirts in the goods area before the crowds peak.
experience.tip: Buy digital tickets in advance only. Saturday gets the most people; enter at opening and see the biggest booths first.

title: Up Garage used parts, Sapporo
titleJa: アップガレージ 札幌
summary: Up Garage is a big chain of used car parts shops: wheels, steering wheels, shift knobs, JDM small parts. Several stores are in Sapporo.
why: Good place for cheap JDM souvenirs (shift knobs, badges) on the last Sapporo day.
cost: Free to browse
winterNote: Stores are in the suburbs; go by car or taxi. Check each store's hours.

experience.hook: Dig through used JDM parts bins for cheap car souvenirs.
moments: Walk rows of used wheels stacked by size and brand.
Look through the steering wheels, shift knobs and gauges in the small parts shelves.
Find old badges, mirror parts or a shift knob that fits in your suitcase.
Compare prices on the tags; used parts here are often far cheaper than new.
experience.tip: Check the store's stock and hours online before you take a taxi out. Check your home country's customs rules for car parts.

title: Toyota Automobile Museum, Nagoya
titleJa: トヨタ博物館
summary: Large museum of about 140 cars from all makers in the world, plus Japanese car history. It is in Nagakute, east of Nagoya.
why: Only worth it if the route changes to go via Nagoya (for example flying out of Nagoya).
cost: Adult fee: check official site (about ¥1,200 in past years)
winterNote: Open 9:30–17:00, closed Mondays. Far from the current route.

experience.hook: About 150 cars from all makers, with the Toyota 2000GT as the star.
moments: Ride the Linimo maglev line to Geidai-dori station and walk to the museum.
Walk the Car Hall, from early European cars to Japanese cars, about 150 in total.
Stand at the white Toyota 2000GT, Japan's classic 1960s sports car.
See the special show on Japan's motorization, open until Feb 28, 2027.
Eat in the museum restaurant or café before you leave.
experience.tip: Closed Mondays. Arrive at 09:30 opening for empty halls. Only worth it if you fly in or out of Nagoya.

title: Shirakawa-go light-up, then fly north
titleJa: 白川郷ライトアップ・飛騨高山・金沢
summary: Replace Tohoku with Takayama old town, the Shirakawa-go winter light-up on Sun Jan 24, 2027, and Kanazawa. On day 8 fly from Komatsu (ANA 11:25 or 14:10) or Toyama (ANA 12:45) to New Chitose, then drive to Niseko on day 9.
why: Snow-covered thatched farmhouses lit at night are one of the most famous winter views in Japan, and the Jan 24 date falls exactly on baseline day 6.
cost: Light-up bus from Takayama 13,000–16,000 (incl. entry); Tokyo→Takayama ~15,000; flight Komatsu→Sapporo ~20,000–35,000
winterNote: 2027 light-up days: Jan 11, 17, 24, 31, 17:30–19:30. Full advance reservation, no tickets on the day. Nouhi bus tours from Takayama go on sale online Oct 13–Nov 2, 2026 (staggered); inn-with-deck-ticket lottery Oct 1–31, 2026. No regular bus back to Takayama after the event, so book a tour that returns. Hakodate (baseline day 8–9) is skipped.

experience.hook: Thatched farmhouses glowing in deep snow, one of four nights a year.
moments: Walk Takayama's old Sanmachi streets and eat Hida beef nigiri served on a rice cracker at a street stand.
Ride the evening tour bus to Shirakawa-go as snow falls on the steep thatched roofs.
Climb 20 minutes to the Shiroyama deck at 17:30 and watch the whole village light up below.
Eat a seafood rice bowl at Kanazawa's Omicho Market, then see rope 'snow umbrellas' on Kenrokuen pines.
Fly from Komatsu to New Chitose and land in Hokkaido snow.
experience.tip: Book the Nouhi bus 'Course B': it is the only tour with a deck ticket. Bring a flashlight; it gets to −10°C.

title: Snow monkeys and Shiga Kogen ski
titleJa: 地獄谷野猿公苑・志賀高原・渋温泉
summary: Take the Hokuriku Shinkansen to Nagano, walk 35–40 min through snow to see wild monkeys in a hot spring, and stay in Shibu or Yudanaka onsen town. Ski Shiga Kogen (or Nozawa Onsen) the next day, then go back via Omiya and take the Hayabusa to Shin-Hakodate on day 8.
why: It replaces Zao with a ski-plus-onsen stop that also has the famous snow monkeys, and Shiga Kogen has easy runs for Aoki and big terrain for Pegasis.
cost: Snow monkey park 800; Nagano→park bus 1,400; lift ticket ~7,000–8,000 (Nozawa 2025–26: 7,500); onsen inn 15,000–25,000
winterNote: Monkey park winter hours 9:00–16:00, arrive 30 min before close; may close for weather. Winter access (Dec 1–Mar 31) changes, check the official site. Monkeys bathe mainly in the coldest months, so late Jan is good. Day 8 Nagano→Omiya→Shin-Hakodate is a long rail day (~6 h).

experience.hook: Wild monkeys soaking in a steaming hot spring while snow falls on them.
moments: Walk about 40 minutes on an icy forest trail to Jigokudani Monkey Park.
Stand at the rock pool and watch red-faced monkeys soak, groom and nap in the steam.
Walk Shibu Onsen's old lantern-lit street in a yukata and hop between its nine public baths.
Ski Shiga Kogen: gentle runs for Aoki, big linked terrain for Pegasis.
experience.tip: Wear boots with grip or rent crampons; the trail is ice. Go early morning, before tour groups arrive.

title: Japan Alps: Matsumoto, Hakuba, Kanazawa
titleJa: 松本城・白馬・金沢
summary: Limited express Azusa from Shinjuku to Matsumoto Castle in snow, then bus to Hakuba for a full ski day at Happo-one. Continue via Nagano to Kanazawa on the Hokuriku Shinkansen and fly Komatsu→Sapporo.
why: Hakuba is a world-class ski area for Pegasis, Matsumoto is one of Japan's original castles, and it removes the long Tohoku rail days.
cost: Matsumoto Castle 1,300 (1,200 e-ticket); Hakuba lift ~8,000–10,000 (not verified for 2026–27); Komatsu→Sapporo flight ~20,000–35,000
winterNote: Castle open 8:30–17:00 every day except Dec 29–31. Past winters had a castle projection-mapping show in the evenings (2025–26: Dec 13–Feb 15); 2027 dates not yet announced. Happo-one 2026–27 prices not found yet.

places.ja: 白馬八方尾根スキー場

experience.hook: A black samurai castle in snow, then ski an Olympic downhill run.
moments: Take your shoes off and climb Matsumoto Castle's steep 61-degree wooden stairs inside Japan's oldest five-storey castle tower.
Ski Hakuba Happo-one, the downhill venue of the 1998 Nagano Olympics, with the Northern Alps all around.
Walk Kanazawa's Higashi Chaya teahouse street and eat a soft-serve ice cream covered in gold leaf.
Eat fresh crab or a seafood bowl at Omicho Market before the flight north.
experience.tip: Come back to Matsumoto Castle after dark: in past winters, free light shows ran on the castle walls from 18:00.

title: Gala Yuzawa Shinkansen ski day
titleJa: GALA湯沢スキー場
summary: Take the Joetsu Shinkansen from Tokyo straight to Gala Yuzawa station, which opens directly into the ski resort gondola. Ski all day with rental gear, soak in the onsen at the base, and be back in Tokyo in the evening.
why: It is the easiest real ski day from Tokyo (about 75–90 min), with beginner slopes for Aoki, and it can replace the long trip to Zao.
cost: Lift 1-day 7,300 (2025–26); Shinkansen ~7,000 each way; JR 'SKISKI' packs can be cheaper
winterNote: 2025–26 season ran Dec 20–May 6; 2026–27 dates not yet published. Gala Yuzawa station runs only in ski season. Weekends are crowded; Jan 24–25 is Sun–Mon.

experience.hook: Step off the bullet train and walk straight into the ski rental shop.
moments: Ride the Joetsu Shinkansen from Tokyo about 75 minutes to Gala Yuzawa station, which is the ski center.
Pick up pre-booked skis, then ride the gondola up to the snow.
Ski 16 courses, up to 2,500 m long, and link to the Ishiuchi Maruyama area for more terrain.
Soak sore legs at SPA Gala no Yu in the station building before the train back.
experience.tip: Book rentals online and pay ¥1,000 for the 'PICK UP BOX' to skip the rental queue. Avoid weekends.

title: Fujiten ski with Fuji view
titleJa: ふじてんスノーリゾート
summary: Small ski resort on the north side of Mt Fuji, about 20 min by car from Lake Kawaguchi. Aoki can take a beginner lesson while Pegasis skis, with Mt Fuji right above the slopes.
why: It adds skiing to the Fuji days and gives Aoki an easy first day before the bigger resorts in Hokkaido.
cost: Lift 1-day 5,500 weekday / 6,500 weekend (2025–26); rental extra
winterNote: 2025–26 season: Dec 13–Apr 1, lifts 9:00–16:30, night ski on weekends/holidays until 21:00. Jan 23 (day 5) is a Saturday, so night ski is possible. Snow is mostly machine-made.

experience.hook: Learn to ski with Mt Fuji filling the sky above the slope.
moments: Drive 20 minutes from Lake Kawaguchi, park, and rent gear at the base.
Take a beginner lesson with the ski school while the other skis the upper runs.
Ride the observation lift to the deck for a close, big view of Mt Fuji.
Stay for night skiing on Saturday, with lights on the slope until 21:00.
experience.tip: Go on a weekday: lift ticket is ¥1,000 cheaper and parking is free.

title: Diamond Fuji sunset at Yamanaka
titleJa: 山中湖 ダイヤモンド富士
summary: At Lake Yamanaka the sun sets exactly on the top of Mt Fuji from mid Oct to late Feb, and the place moves around the lake each day. In late Jan it is seen from the north shore (Oike beach, Nagaike) at about 15:55–16:15.
why: A short, free photo stop that fits the Fuji day after the Hakone drive, and it is one of the best-known winter Fuji views.
cost: free
winterNote: Official list: Oike beach until ~Jan 30 (~16:03), Yanagashiri until ~Jan 27 (~15:55), Nagaike lakeside until ~Feb 5 (~16:13). Needs clear sky; check the exact spot for Jan 22/23 on the Yamanakako site.

experience.hook: The setting sun sits exactly on Fuji's peak like a diamond ring.
moments: Drive to Lake Yamanaka's north shore at about 15:00 and park in a proper lot.
Stand at Oike beach, where white swans swim in front of Mt Fuji.
Watch the sun touch the summit around 16:00 and flash for a few seconds.
Look down at calm water for a second diamond reflected in the lake.
experience.tip: The lake is at 1,000 m; after sunset it gets very cold fast. Bring gloves and a hot drink.

title: Lake Motosu and lava ice caves
titleJa: 本栖湖・鳴沢氷穴・富岳風穴
summary: Walk into Narusawa Ice Cave and Fugaku Wind Cave, lava tubes in the Aokigahara forest where ice stays all year. Then drive to Lake Motosu, the view of Mt Fuji printed on the 1,000-yen note.
why: Aoki can drive the quiet lake roads west of Kawaguchiko, and it is a different Fuji view from Chureito with few people.
cost: Each cave ~350–500 (check); free lake
winterNote: Cave temperature 0–3°C all year. Winter opening hours were not confirmed; check the official site. Lake roads can be icy early in the morning.

experience.hook: Crawl into a frozen lava tube, then see the view on Japan's money.
moments: Walk down into Narusawa Ice Cave and see ice pillars that grow from ceiling drips in winter.
Duck through a passage only 91 cm high, at 0–4°C.
Walk the forest path over mossy lava to Fugaku Wind Cave next door.
Drive to Lake Motosu and hold a 1,000-yen note up to the real Fuji.
experience.tip: Winter and early spring have the biggest ice pillars. Each cave takes about 15 minutes; wear a hat.

title: Fuji-Q rides and ice skating
titleJa: 富士急ハイランド
summary: Theme park at the foot of Mt Fuji with extreme roller coasters and a 400 m outdoor skating rink (SEIKO-OVAL) in winter. Ride coasters with Mt Fuji in view, then skate with rental skates.
why: It is next to Kawaguchiko station, so it fits the Fuji days with no extra travel.
cost: Rink or free-pass tickets: check official site (not verified)
winterNote: Outdoor rink open early Dec to late Feb. Some coasters stop in strong wind or snow.

experience.hook: Skate a 400 m outdoor ice oval under Mt Fuji.
moments: Ride Fujiyama or Takabisha and see Mt Fuji from the top of the lift hill.
Rent skates and skate SEIKO-OVAL, a full 400 m outdoor speed-skating rink.
Glide laps in the cold air with Mt Fuji in view.
Walk a few minutes to Kawaguchiko for hot food after.
experience.tip: Coasters stop in strong wind; ride them first, in the calm morning, and skate in the afternoon.

title: Owakudani and Open-Air Museum
titleJa: 大涌谷・箱根彫刻の森美術館
summary: Ride the Hakone Ropeway over the steaming volcanic valley of Owakudani and eat the black eggs cooked in the hot springs. Stop at the Hakone Open-Air Museum, a large sculpture park with a foot bath.
why: It fits between the Hakone Turnpike drive and Kawaguchiko, with Mt Fuji views from the ropeway on clear winter days.
cost: Ropeway ~1,500–2,500 one way; museum ~2,000 (check)
winterNote: Ropeway Dec–Jan 9:00–16:15; it stops in wind of 30 m/s or more and has yearly maintenance closures, so check the operation page.

experience.hook: Fly over a steaming volcano crater and eat eggs boiled black in it.
moments: Ride the Hakone Ropeway from Sounzan, 130 m above a valley full of yellow sulfur steam.
Eat a black egg at Owakudani; locals say each one adds seven years to your life.
Look for Mt Fuji from the ropeway toward Lake Ashi on a clear day.
Walk into the 18 m stained-glass tower at the Hakone Open-Air Museum, then warm your feet in the hot-spring foot bath.
experience.tip: In December–January the ropeway stops at 16:15. Go in the morning, when Fuji is most often clear.

title: Gotemba outlets with Fuji view
titleJa: 御殿場プレミアム・アウトレット
summary: Large outlet mall on the east side of Mt Fuji, on the road from Hakone to Kawaguchiko. Shop for ski wear and brand goods with Fuji in the background.
why: It is directly on the day 4 driving route and is a cheap place to buy winter gear before the ski days.
cost: free entry
winterNote: Open all winter; the Fuji view is best on clear mornings.
sources: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/御殿場プレミアム・アウトレット

experience.hook: Buy cheap ski wear with Mt Fuji right behind the shops.
moments: Walk the 290 outlet shops and look for ski jackets, gloves and thermal wear.
Cross the 'Yume no Kakehashi' bridge to the Hill Side area for a big Fuji view.
Eat lunch at the food court between shops.
Soak in Konohana-no-yu, the onsen next to the outlets, before driving on.
experience.tip: Arrive at 10:00 opening: fewer people, and Fuji is usually clearer in the morning.

title: Atami plum garden and Izu drive
titleJa: 熱海梅園・伊豆スカイライン
summary: Aoki drives from Hakone down to Atami, a seaside onsen town, and sees early plum blossoms at Atami Baien. The Izu Skyline toll road along the mountain ridge is an extra option with sea and Fuji views.
why: A car-focused day with onsen and early flowers, close to the Hakone Turnpike.
cost: Plum festival entry ~300 (check); car rental and tolls extra
winterNote: 2026 plum festival ran Jan 10–Mar 8; 2027 dates not yet published, likely similar. Kawazu cherry festival 2027 is Feb 6–Mar 7, so it is AFTER this trip. Ridge roads can be icy in the morning.

experience.hook: Japan's earliest plum blossoms, then a ridge road above the sea.
moments: Drive down from Hakone to Atami, with the Pacific opening up below.
Walk Atami Baien among 469 plum trees of 60 kinds, some over 100 years old.
Rest your feet in the garden's foot bath; some days there is free amazake.
Drive the Izu Skyline ridge road for sea views and Fuji on clear days.
experience.tip: Early-bloom trees flower first; in late January expect part bloom. Drive the Skyline after late morning, when ice melts.

title: Kusatsu Onsen night in snow
titleJa: 草津温泉
summary: Direct highway bus from Tokyo (Yaesu 7:10, arrives 11:35) to Kusatsu, one of Japan's top onsen towns. See the steaming Yubatake hot-water field lit at night, watch the yumomi water-cooling show, and ski at Kusatsu Onsen ski area.
why: Strong onsen town with snow and light skiing, and a simpler, closer alternative to Zao.
cost: Bus ~3,500–4,500 each way (check); yumomi show 700; ryokan 15,000–25,000
winterNote: Yumomi show 6 times a day at Netsu-no-yu. Paths around Yubatake freeze, wear good shoes. From Kusatsu, going north to Hokkaido means back through Tokyo/Omiya.

experience.hook: A town-square river of steaming hot water, lit up at night in snow.
moments: Stand at the Yubatake, where boiling spring water runs down wooden channels in clouds of steam.
Watch the yumomi show at Netsu-no-yu: women stir hot water with long wooden boards and sing.
Soak in the big Sai-no-kawara open-air bath with snow on the rocks around you.
Ski the Kusatsu Onsen ski area on Mt Tengu, over 90 years old.
Walk back to the Yubatake after dark, when lights shine through the steam and snow.
experience.tip: The water is very acidic; rinse before bed and take off silver jewelry before you soak.

title: Gokayama Ainokura quiet window lights
titleJa: 五箇山 相倉合掌造り集落
summary: Smaller, quieter thatched-roof village than Shirakawa-go, in deep snow. On Wed Jan 27, 2027 there is a 'window light' evening (17:00–20:00) where you see the village at night with house lights only.
why: A calm backup if Shirakawa-go light-up tickets are sold out, and it fits a Hokuriku route.
cost: free village entry; parking fee
winterNote: Main 2027 winter light-up is Feb 20–21 (after the trip). Window-light days: Jan 13 and Jan 27, 2027. Jan 27 only fits if the Hokuriku plan is shifted by 1 day.

experience.hook: A snowed-in thatched village lit only by the windows of people living there.
moments: Walk into Ainokura in deep snow, with about 20 thatched houses and almost no crowds.
Try Gokayama tofu, a local tofu so firm it can be tied with rope.
Walk up to the viewpoint near the parking lot at dusk.
Watch warm window lights come on across the snow roofs, open until 20:00.
experience.tip: It is only on Jan 13 and Jan 27, 2027. Wear snow boots; paths are not cleared everywhere.

title: East Hokkaido drift ice road trip
titleJa: 道東ドライブ（網走・知床・摩周・阿寒・鶴居）
summary: Fly New Chitose to Memanbetsu, rent a 4WD car and drive Abashiri (icebreaker Aurora) → Utoro/Shiretoko → Lake Mashu and Lake Kussharo swans → Lake Akan Ainu Kotan → Tsurui red-crowned cranes, then fly out of Kushiro. It replaces baseline days 11–14 (Otaru, Asahikawa, Biei, Furano, Sapporo).
why: Aoki can drive, you get the wildest winter scenery in Japan (sea ice, cranes, frozen lakes, onsen towns), and Kushiro has direct flights to Haneda for Pegasis on Feb 1.
cost: about ¥60,000–80,000 pp (domestic flights ¥10,000–20,000 each way, 4WD rental ~¥12,000/day shared, Aurora ¥7,000, onsen hotels ¥10,000–18,000)
winterNote: Day plan: D11 Jan29 Niseko→New Chitose (~2 h) fly to Memanbetsu, Abashiri. D12 Jan30 Aurora icebreaker 9:00/11:00, drive Abashiri→Utoro (~75 km, ~1 h 20 min). D13 Jan31 Utoro→Shari→Lake Mashu 1st observatory→Sunayu swans on Lake Kussharo→Akan onsen (~200 km, ~3.5–4 h driving). D14 Feb1 Akan→Tsurumidai cranes (~1 h)→Kushiro airport (~30 min), fly. Drift ice: Abashiri first sighting 2026 was Jan 22, shore contact Feb 1 (3 days earlier than normal); in late Jan ice may still be offshore or absent. Shiretoko Pass (Utoro↔Rausu) is closed all winter. Guided drift ice walks (e.g. SHINRA) start Feb 1. Akan ice festival 2026 ran Feb 1–Mar 1, so fireworks may not have started by Jan 31. Safety: rentals in Hokkaido come with studless tyres, ask for 4WD; drive only in daylight (sunset ~16:15), roads can be ice-covered and whiteouts happen on open farmland (e.g. near Shari/Koshimizu); check road info before each day and keep 30–50% extra time. Aoki should be the main driver.

places.ja: 網走流氷観光砕氷船おーろら（道の駅 流氷街道網走）
道の駅 うとろ・シリエトク

experience.hook: Four days of sea ice, frozen lakes, wild swans and dancing cranes by 4WD.
moments: Stand on the deck of the Aurora icebreaker in Abashiri and hear sea ice crack under the hull.
Drive the Okhotsk coast to Utoro and watch the sea turn white near Oronko Rock at sunset.
Look down into frozen Lake Mashu from the 1st Observatory, a round blue-white bowl in the mountains.
Dig into the warm sand at Sunayu on Lake Kussharo while whooper swans float on the steaming water.
Watch red-crowned cranes call and dance in the snow at Tsurumidai before your Kushiro flight.
experience.tip: Drive only in daylight, sunset is about 16:15. Book the first Aurora sailing: fewer people on the bow deck.

title: Asahikawa to Abashiri via Sounkyo
titleJa: 旭川→層雲峡→網走 ドライブ
summary: Keep the baseline up to the Asahiyama Zoo, then drive east: night at Sounkyo Onsen for the Ice Waterfall Festival, next day over Sekihoku Pass to Abashiri for the Aurora icebreaker, then fly home side from Memanbetsu. It replaces Biei/Furano/Sapporo (days 12 afternoon–14).
why: A shorter, lower-risk taste of the east: ice festival, onsen, and a chance of sea ice, with only two driving days.
cost: about ¥45,000–60,000 pp (car ~¥12,000/day shared, Sounkyo ryokan ¥12,000–20,000, festival ¥1,000, Aurora ¥7,000, flight Memanbetsu→Haneda ¥15,000–30,000)
winterNote: Sounkyo Ice Waterfall Festival 2027: Jan 23–Mar 7 (weekday 17:00–21:30, weekend from 11:00). Asahikawa→Sounkyo about 70 km (~1 h 15 min); Sounkyo→Abashiri about 160 km (~2 h 45 min) over Sekihoku Pass, which is a mountain pass with snow and ice, drive in daylight only. Drift ice in Abashiri is not sure in late Jan (2026: first sighting Jan 22). Aurora runs Jan 20–Mar 31 (2027 plan). Memanbetsu airport is ~25 min from Abashiri.

places.ja: 道の駅 流氷街道網走

experience.hook: Glowing ice towers, a hot onsen, then an icebreaker on the Okhotsk Sea.
moments: Drive east from Asahikawa into the Sounkyo gorge, with cliffs and frozen waterfalls beside the road.
Walk through lit ice tunnels and towers at the Ice Waterfall Festival, then soak in your hotel onsen.
Cross Sekihoku Pass in morning light, through white forest with almost no other cars.
Ride the Aurora icebreaker out of Abashiri for one hour, looking for sea ice and eagles.
experience.tip: Leave Sounkyo early; the pass needs daylight. Check the Japan Coast Guard drift ice map the night before the cruise.

title: Shift trip for Sapporo Snow Festival
titleJa: さっぽろ雪まつり
summary: Move the whole 15-day trip 9 days later (Thu Jan 28 – Thu Feb 11, 2027) so the Hokkaido week (days 8–14 = Feb 4–10) falls inside the Sapporo Snow Festival (Feb 4–11). The Asahikawa Winter Festival (Feb 6–11) then also lines up with days 11–12.
why: Giant snow sculptures at Odori, ice sculptures in Susukino, and snow slides at Tsudome, plus a better chance of drift ice in February.
cost: no entry fee; Sapporo hotels in festival week cost much more and sell out early (plan ¥15,000–30,000 per room per night, book now)
winterNote: 2027 Snow Festival: Feb 4 (Thu)–Feb 11 (Thu, holiday), Odori, Tsudome and Susukino sites. Aoki's 15-day visa limit: Jan 28–Feb 11 inclusive is exactly 15 days, so do not add a day. Flights are not booked yet, so this is still possible. Tokyo/Zao parts shift too (Zao snow monsters are still good in early Feb).

places.ja: 旭川冬まつり（常磐公園周辺）

experience.hook: Move nine days and Sapporo turns into a city of giant snow buildings.
moments: Walk the Odori Park blocks past five huge snow sculptures, some the size of real buildings.
Watch light shows projected onto the big snow sculptures after dark.
Walk the Susukino ice sculptures at night, with ramen and bars on every side.
Slide down long snow slides at the Tsudome site like kids.
Take a day trip to the Asahikawa Winter Festival and its giant snow stage.
experience.tip: Go up the Sapporo TV Tower at the east end of Odori for the full view of the sculptures. Book hotels now.

title: Lake Shikotsu Ice Festival
titleJa: 千歳・支笏湖氷濤まつり
summary: Walk-through ice sculptures and ice caves made from blue lake water, lit in many colours after dark. It is 40 min by car from New Chitose Airport, so it fits the last Sapporo day.
why: It opens on Jan 30, 2027, just in time for your last Hokkaido days, and it is easy to reach on the way to the airport.
cost: ¥1,000 weekdays, ¥3,000 weekends/holidays
winterNote: 2027: Jan 30 (Sat)–Feb 23 (Tue), 10:00–20:00, light-up 16:30–20:00. Jan 30–31 are weekend (¥3,000); Feb 1 is Monday (¥1,000). Bus from JR Chitose Station about 60 min.

experience.hook: Ice caves made of clear lake water, blue by day, rainbow-lit at night.
moments: Walk into ice caves and towers made by spraying Lake Shikotsu water onto frames until it freezes.
Look at the natural 'Shikotsu blue' of the ice in the afternoon light.
Stay as the colored lights switch on at 16:30 and the ice glows.
Listen to the ice creak in the cold, then warm up in a Shikotsu onsen nearby.
experience.tip: Arrive about 15:30 to see the blue ice and the lights in one visit. Monday Feb 1 costs ¥1,000, not ¥3,000.

title: Tomamu Ice Village and ski
titleJa: 星野リゾート トマム アイスヴィレッジ
summary: A small town of ice domes at Hoshino Resorts Tomamu with an ice bar, ice skating, ice slide and ice restaurant, open in the evening. By day, ski Tomamu and ride to the Frost Tree Terrace (霧氷テラス) at 1,088 m.
why: Fits between Furano and Sapporo, gives Pegasis good ski runs and Aoki easy runs, and the ice bar is a fun evening.
cost: Ice Village ¥600 (free for resort guests); ice bar from ¥1,500; lift pass extra
winterNote: Ice Village 2026-27: Dec 20, 2026–Mar 10, 2027 (planned), 17:00–22:00. Frost Tree Terrace and ski: Dec 1, 2026–Apr 5, 2027. The summer Unkai (sea of clouds) Terrace is NOT open in winter. Furano→Tomamu ~1 h, Tomamu→Sapporo ~2 h by expressway.

experience.hook: Ski by day, then drink from a glass made of ice at night.
moments: Ride the gondola to the Frost Tree Terrace at 1,088 m and see trees coated in white frost.
Ski Tomamu's wide groomed runs: fast ones for the good skier, easy ones for the beginner.
Walk the Ice Village at night: ice dome hotel, ice chapel, ice rink with light projections.
Drink at the Ice Bar from an ice glass, then ride the ice slide down.
Eat ice cheese fondue or the 'iceberg' bouillabaisse at the Ice Restaurant.
experience.tip: Go up to the Frost Tree Terrace early on a cold, clear morning; the frost on the trees melts later in the day.

title: Sounkyo Ice Waterfall Festival
titleJa: 層雲峡温泉氷瀑まつり
summary: Ice towers, tunnels and an ice shrine built by the river in the Sounkyo gorge, lit up at night. Stay in a Sounkyo onsen hotel or do an evening trip from Asahikawa.
why: Ice festival plus onsen in one stop, only ~1 h 15 min from Asahikawa where you already stay.
cost: ¥1,000 entry; onsen hotel ¥12,000–20,000 with dinner
winterNote: 52nd festival 2027: Jan 23 (Sat)–Mar 7 (Sun). Weekdays 17:00–21:30, weekends/holidays 11:00–21:30.

experience.hook: Walk through glowing ice tunnels in a gorge, then soak in hot spring water.
moments: Enter the festival site by the river and walk under tall ice towers lit in blue, green and red.
Go through the ice tunnels and visit the small ice shrine.
Feel the gorge air at about -15°C while your breath freezes on your scarf.
Walk back to your hotel and soak in the onsen with snow falling outside.
experience.tip: Stay the night in Sounkyo so you can visit late, after 20:00, when the crowds are small. Wear shoes with grip.

title: Garinko icebreaker at Mombetsu
titleJa: 流氷砕氷船ガリンコ号III IMERU
summary: A 1-hour cruise on an icebreaker with big drills at the bow that cut through drift ice off Mombetsu. From Asahikawa it is about 2 h 30 min by car on the Asahikawa-Mombetsu expressway, or fly Haneda–Mombetsu.
why: The drift-ice boat closest to your baseline route (Asahikawa), for a unique winter sight.
cost: about ¥4,000 (2026 adult fare)
winterNote: 2026 season ran Jan 13–Mar 28. 2027 bookings open Oct 9, 2026. Ice near Mombetsu usually comes in late Jan–Feb; before that the cruise sails on open sea. Cruises can be cancelled for bad weather.

experience.hook: A ship with two giant screw drills that grinds its way through sea ice.
moments: Board Garinko III IMERU at Mombetsu port and walk to the bow deck.
Watch the two red screw drills at the front roll onto the ice and crush it.
Hear the grinding and cracking as white ice plates split into blue sea water.
Visit the Okhotsk Tower after the cruise, an observatory that stands out in the sea.
experience.tip: Book when 2027 reservations open on Oct 9, 2026. Stand at the bow rail early; it is the best spot to see the drills.

title: Lake Toya and Noboribetsu Hells
titleJa: 洞爺湖温泉・登別地獄谷
summary: Instead of Onuma→Niseko, drive Hakodate→Lake Toya (lakeside onsen, view of Showa-Shinzan) and on to Noboribetsu, walking the steaming Jigokudani 'Hell Valley' and soaking in a big onsen hotel. Continue to Rusutsu for ski the next day.
why: Japan's most famous onsen town plus a volcano lake, a good change if you want more onsen and less ski.
cost: Jigokudani free (parking fee); onsen hotel ¥12,000–25,000 with dinner
winterNote: Hakodate→Toya about 2 h 30 min, Toya→Noboribetsu about 1 h by car. Jigokudani paths can be icy, wear shoe spikes. Toya Onsen normally has short nightly fireworks in winter too; 2027 schedule not checked.

experience.hook: A volcano lake onsen, then a steaming valley that smells of sulfur.
moments: Soak in a lakeside onsen at Toya and look out at the dark water and snowy Showa-Shinzan volcano.
Watch the short winter fireworks over Lake Toya from your room, if they run in 2027.
Walk the boardwalk through Jigokudani 'Hell Valley', with steam vents and the smell of sulfur all around.
See the red oni demon statues around Noboribetsu town and the Enma statue at Enmado.
Try many baths from different hot springs in one big Noboribetsu onsen hotel.
experience.tip: Walk Jigokudani early in the morning; in the cold the steam is thicker and the path is empty. Bring shoe spikes.

title: Rusutsu, Kiroro, Teine, Furano ski
titleJa: ルスツ・キロロ・サッポロテイネ・富良野スキー場
summary: Other ski areas on the baseline route: Rusutsu (big, fewer crowds than Niseko), Kiroro (very deep snow, between Otaru and Niseko), Sapporo Teine (40 min from Sapporo, 1972 Olympic runs) and Furano (on day 13). Each has good beginner slopes and ski school for Aoki.
why: More ski time for Pegasis without changing the route; Teine lets you ski on the last Sapporo day.
cost: 1-day lift pass about ¥7,000–¥13,000 (2025-26 prices, Rusutsu/Kiroro higher); rental ¥5,000–7,000
winterNote: Late January is peak powder season in Hokkaido. Lift prices for 2026-27 not yet checked.

experience.hook: Deep January powder at four resorts, each with easy runs for beginners.
moments: Ride through the trees at Rusutsu, with three mountains and far fewer people than Niseko.
Ski the deep, soft snow at Kiroro, one of the snowiest resorts in Hokkaido.
Ski down Sapporo Teine's Olympic runs with the sea and Sapporo city below you.
Take the Furano ropeway up and look out over the snowy Tokachi mountains.
experience.tip: Book a half-day ski school lesson for the beginner in the morning; the good skier explores, then meet for lunch.

title: Nikka Yoichi and Tenguyama
titleJa: ニッカウヰスキー余市蒸溜所・小樽天狗山
summary: On the Otaru day, visit the Nikka Yoichi whisky distillery (free guided tour with tasting, about 1 h) and ride the Tenguyama ropeway for a view over Otaru and the sea; Tenguyama also has a small ski area.
why: Whisky and a snowy harbour view on a day that is mostly driving; Yoichi is only ~30 min west of Otaru.
cost: distillery tour free; Tenguyama ropeway about ¥1,600–2,000 round trip (not checked for 2027)
winterNote: Nikka tour: online booking only, opens about 1 month before, no same-day entry; closed Dec 23–Jan 7 (so late Jan is open). The driver cannot taste. Tenguyama ropeway runs in winter; check for wind stops.

places.ja: ニッカウヰスキー余市蒸溜所
天狗山ロープウェイ山麓駅

experience.hook: Whisky made over coal fires, then Otaru harbor lights from a mountain top.
moments: Walk the red-roof stone buildings of Nikka Yoichi, the first Nikka distillery, from 1934.
Watch the pot stills heated by coal fire, the same old method founder Taketsuru learned in Scotland.
See Taketsuru's old house, then taste the free Nikka samples at the end of the tour.
Ride the Tenguyama ropeway at dusk and rub the tengu's long nose for luck.
Look down at Otaru harbor lights, one of Hokkaido's three famous night views.
experience.tip: Book the Nikka tour online about one month before; there is no same-day entry. The driver gets soft drinks.

title: Sapporo ramen, beer and shrine
titleJa: 元祖さっぽろラーメン横丁・サッポロビール博物館・北海道神宮
summary: Morning at snowy Hokkaido Shrine in Maruyama Park, afternoon at the Sapporo Beer Museum (tasting, Genghis Khan lamb BBQ at the Beer Garden next door), evening miso ramen in the Ganso Ramen Yokocho alley in Susukino.
why: An easy, low-cost last day in the city with the three classic Sapporo tastes before Pegasis flies.
cost: about ¥5,000–8,000 pp for food and drink; shrine free
winterNote: All open in winter. Beer Museum tasting is paid; check hours before (not verified for 2027).

places.ja: サッポロビール博物館
元祖さっぽろラーメン横丁

experience.hook: Snowy shrine, beer in red brick, and miso ramen: three Sapporo classics.
moments: Walk through Maruyama Park's snowy forest to Hokkaido Jingu and its quiet wooden shrine.
Eat a warm grilled mochi 'Hangan-sama' at the teahouse inside the shrine grounds.
Taste beer in the red-brick Sapporo Beer Museum, including a beer you can only drink there.
Grill Genghis Khan lamb on a dome-shaped iron pan at the Sapporo Beer Garden next door.
End in Ganso Ramen Yokocho in Susukino with a bowl of rich miso ramen with butter and corn.
experience.tip: Book a Beer Garden table for early dinner, then walk off the lamb before ramen. Your clothes will smell of lamb.

title: Jozankei Onsen night
titleJa: 定山渓温泉
summary: Sapporo's own onsen town in a snowy river valley, about 1 h from the city by bus or car. Stay one night between Furano and the flight instead of a business hotel.
why: A proper onsen night close to Sapporo and New Chitose, good last night for both of you.
cost: onsen hotel about ¥12,000–25,000 pp with dinner
winterNote: The snow candle event Yukitouro ran Jan 27–Feb 3, 2026 at Jozankei Shrine and was called the FINAL edition in this form; organisers say a new 'yukitouro' will come later. 2027 dates and form are unknown.

experience.hook: Sapporo's onsen town in a snowy river valley, one hour from the city.
moments: Take the bus from Sapporo into the deep valley as the snow gets thicker.
Walk the river path to the red Futami suspension bridge over a steaming stream.
Look for the green kappa water-spirit statues all around town.
Soak your feet in the free public foot bath, then soak in your hotel's river-view open-air bath.
experience.tip: Book the Kappa Liner bus from Sapporo. Get a room with dinner included; the town has few restaurants at night.

title: Lake Akan Ainu Kotan and cranes
titleJa: 阿寒湖アイヌコタン・鶴見台
summary: At Lake Akan, see the Ainu village street and an Ainu dance or the 'Lost Kamuy' show, and walk on the frozen lake (snowmobile, banana boat, fireworks during the ice festival). Next morning drive to Tsurui to watch wild red-crowned cranes at a feeding site.
why: Ainu culture and famous cranes are things you cannot see anywhere else in Japan.
duration: 1–2 days (part of an east Hokkaido plan)
cost: Ainu theatre about ¥2,000–4,000 (not verified); festival free; crane viewing free or small donation
winterNote: Akan ice festival 'ICE・愛す・阿寒 冬華美' 2026: Feb 1–Mar 1 (fireworks 20:00; ice surface activities in that period); 2027 dates not yet out. Cranes gather at winter feeding sites in Tsurui from about Nov to Mar (feeding times not verified). Akan→Tsurumidai about 1 h.

places.ja: 鶴居・伊藤タンチョウサンクチュアリ

experience.hook: Ainu songs by a frozen lake, then wild cranes dancing in the snow.
moments: Walk the Akan Ainu Kotan street, full of carved wood shops, in a village of about 120 Ainu people.
Watch 'Lost Kamuy' at the Ainu Theater Ikor, a show with Ainu dance and digital images.
Walk out onto frozen Lake Akan and, in festival time, watch fireworks over the ice.
Watch wild red-crowned cranes call and dance in the snowy field at Tsurumidai.
Stand on Otowa Bridge at dawn to see cranes in the river mist on very cold mornings.
experience.tip: For Otowa Bridge, arrive before sunrise on a day below -15°C; the river steam and frost are strongest then.

title: Cape Kamui on Shakotan
titleJa: 神威岬
summary: A narrow cape on the Shakotan Peninsula with a 770 m ridge path to the tip and very blue sea. From Otaru it is about 2 h by car along the coast.
why: A dramatic coastal drive for Aoki, but mostly a summer place.
cost: free
winterNote: The path to the tip is closed in strong wind, which is common in winter; buses run only Apr–Nov. Winter access to the path not confirmed. Low value in late Jan; not recommended.

experience.hook: A thin rocky cape over a very blue sea, but mostly a summer place.
moments: Drive the Shakotan coast road from Otaru past fishing villages and dark cliffs.
Walk through the old gate at the start of the 770 m ridge path, if the wind lets it open.
Look down at the rocks and the cold winter sea from the path.
experience.tip: In late January the path often closes for wind. Go on a calm day, or skip it and spend the time in Otaru.

title: @home café, classic Akihabara maid café
titleJa: あっとほぉーむカフェ
summary: The best-known maid café chain in Akihabara; maids greet you with 'Welcome home, Master/Princess'. You order food or a drink, the maids cast the 'moe moe kyun' spell on it, and you can buy an instant photo (cheki) with a maid.
why: It is the easiest, most beginner-friendly way to see the maid café culture you see in anime, with English menus and card/Alipay/WeChat payment.
cost: Admission ¥850 (ages 23–59; ¥600 ages 19–22) + at least 1 drink (¥720–900). Drink course incl. cheki ¥1,690; food course ¥2,810; full course ¥3,810. Extra cheki ¥870 (large ¥1,080). Total about ¥2,500–4,700.
