winterNote: Indoor, open all year. Maids change costumes for seasonal 'cos days'. Weekends and evenings have a queue; use the at-Entry queue ticket or at-PASS reservation on the site. Electronic money (IC) payment ends Oct 2026; cards, PayPay, Alipay, WeChat Pay still OK.

places.ja: あっとほぉーむカフェ ドンキ店
あっとほぉーむカフェ AKIBAカルチャーズZONE店

photoQuery: Akihabara maid cafe Don Quijote building

experience.hook: Maids greet you in chorus and draw on your omurice in ketchup.
moments: Hear the whole café call 'Welcome home, Master!' as you step in and get your at-home key card.
Order the Hiyoko-san omurice and ask the maid to draw a picture on it in ketchup.
Make heart hands and chant 'moe moe kyun' with your maid to make the food 'tastier'.
Pick a maid and pose for a cheki photo; she decorates it with drawings at your table.
experience.tip: The Drink Course (¥1,690) already includes one cheki. It is the cheapest full experience if you are not hungry.

title: Maidreamin, maid café with stage shows
titleJa: めいどりーみん 秋葉原本店
summary: Big maid café chain with 7 shops in Akihabara, open until 23:00. Every shop has a small stage where maids sing and dance, and first-timers get a 'Maidreamin passport'.
why: Loud, bright and fun for a first visit, and the late hours fit an evening after a full day of anime spots.
cost: Entry ¥880 per hour (adult) + food/drink. Official average: ¥1,500 soft drink only, ¥2,000–2,500 with food, ¥2,500–3,500 with alcohol and a live show. Photo with a maid is extra.
winterNote: Indoor, open every day. Honten: Mon–Fri 11:30–23:00, Sat/Sun/holidays 10:30–23:00. No table or service charge. Payment: cash, cards, PayPay, WeChat Pay, Alipay. Reservation form on the site.

places.ja: めいどりーみん 秋葉原本店
めいどりーみん Heaven's Gate

experience.hook: Get a passport to the 'dream country' and watch maids perform live.
moments: Receive your Maidreamin passport and choose the name the maids will call you.
Say the spell 'oishiku nare, moe moe kyun' together with the maid over your drink.
Watch a maid song-and-dance show on the small stage between orders.
Take a commemorative photo with the maid you like before you 'leave the country'.
experience.tip: Entry is charged per hour, so order at once and watch the clock. For a bigger show, pick the Heaven's Gate live restaurant.

title: Cure Maid Café, the first maid café
titleJa: キュアメイドカフェ
summary: Opened in 2001, it calls itself Japan's first maid café. It is calm: classic long maid uniforms, good tea and scones, and a changing anime collaboration menu.
why: A quiet, historic spot for anime fans; it appears as a model in 'Love Live!' and 'Saekano' and always runs an anime collab.
cost: No entry charge found on the official site. Tea ¥770; food/collab menus extra. About ¥1,500–3,000.
winterNote: Open 11:00–20:00 daily (food L.O. 19:00). Moved: now in Onoden Bldg 4F (Gee! Store Akiba) by the station. Numbered tickets when busy; seat reservation only for paid 'supporter card' members. Collab cafés change about every 2 weeks; check what runs on Jan 20, 2027.
anime: Love Live! and Saekano (How to Raise a Boring Girlfriend) use it as a model; rotating official anime collab menus

experience.hook: Drink real tea where the maid café started, back in 2001.
moments: Ride the Onoden escalator to 4F and walk through the Gee! Store to the café.
Order a pot of Darjeeling or smoky Lapsang souchong from the tea list, ¥770.
Try a scone or waffle while maids in long classic dresses serve quietly.
Check the collab menu and goods of whatever anime runs that fortnight.
experience.tip: Photos of your food are fine, but keep staff and other guests out of the frame, and no video.

title: Cafe Mai:lish, quiet classic maid café
titleJa: カフェ メイリッシュ
summary: One of the older Akihabara maid cafés, calm and relaxed. No table charge: one order per 90 minutes, and the tea is certified by the Japan Tea Association.
why: A more authentic, less showy maid café for when the loud chains feel too much; no entry fee keeps it cheap.
cost: No table charge; 1 order per 90 min. About ¥1,000–2,500.
winterNote: Closed on Wednesdays, so NOT on day 2 (Wed Jan 20, 2027). Mon/Tue/Thu 14:00–22:00, Fri–Sun/holidays 12:00–22:00. Every Thursday is 'Classical Maid Day' (day 3 evening fits). Phone reservations only on weekdays, up to 1 month ahead; no reservations on weekends.

experience.hook: A calm maid café where nobody rushes you: one order buys 90 minutes.
moments: Climb to the 2nd floor of FH Kyowa Square on Sotokanda 3-chome.
Order tea and scones; on Thursdays the maids wear classic uniforms with a special tea menu.
Charge your phone at the table and rest your legs after the Akihabara crowds.
Collect a stamp for each ¥1,000 you spend on the original stamp card.
experience.tip: Go on Thursday evening (day 3) for Classical Maid Day. Ask staff first before you photograph your food.

title: Swallowtail butler café, Ikebukuro
titleJa: 執事喫茶 スワロウテイル
summary: A Victorian-style tea salon near Otome Road where butlers in tailcoats serve you. You pick your teacup from over 50, and eat a set meal or afternoon tea.
why: The elegant 'reverse' of a maid café, famous in otome and anime culture; men are welcome too.
cost: 1 set per person is required: ¥5,400 (e.g. pasta + salad + drink, or scones + savoury + dessert tea set); dinner course ¥7,900. Cash or credit card only (no e-money).
winterNote: Advance web reservation with an account is required; walk-in only if there is a same-day cancellation ('today's free seats' on the site). Tea time 10:30–18:15, dinner 18:30–21:15. Arrive 50+ min late = refused and cancellation fee. Menu changes monthly; book as soon as January dates open.

experience.hook: A butler opens the door and calls you home to a Victorian mansion.
moments: Wait by the basement entrance until the doorman checks your booking and a butler escorts you in.
Choose your teacup from more than 50 in the cup selection.
Eat the monthly set, like scones with two jams and creams, or seasonal pasta.
Relax to the end; a butler comes 20–30 minutes before your time ends to settle the bill.
experience.tip: Absolutely no photos inside, with no exceptions. Ask the doorman where you may photograph the entrance.

title: Maid idol live show night
titleJa: めいどりーみん LIVE RESTAURANT Heaven's Gate
summary: Maidreamin's 60-seat 'live restaurant' next to Akihabara station, built around a stage. Maids perform idol-style songs and dances while you eat and drink.
why: The closest thing to an idol concert-bar in one easy evening, and it stays open until 23:00.
cost: Entry ¥880 per hour + food/drink; about ¥2,500–3,500 with a drink and a show (official average for 'drinks and live').
winterNote: Open daily: Mon–Fri 11:30–23:00, Sat/Sun/holidays 10:30–23:00. Event nights (birthdays, battles between shops) are the busiest; check the event page for Jan 2027 and reserve on the site.

experience.hook: Eat dinner while maids put on a live idol show on stage.
moments: Take the lift to 6F of the building by the Electric Town exit.
Order a drink and food, then join the 'moe moe kyun' spell with the whole room.
Wave along as maids sing and dance on the stage, like at a small idol live.
Walk out after 22:00 into the lit-up Chuo-dori signs.
experience.tip: Look at the event calendar: a shop 'battle' or a maid's anniversary night gives the biggest show.

title: Otome Road and Animate Café
titleJa: 乙女ロード・アニメイトカフェ池袋
summary: Ikebukuro's Otome Road is the fan street for female anime fans. Eat at an official Animate Café anime collab and drink a 'Gratte' latte with a character printed on the cream.
why: Real anime collab food and goods in one short walk, with the Animate Ikebukuro main store next door.
cost: Collab café: about ¥2,000–3,000 (check each event). Gratte latte: about ¥1,000 (check). No reservation needed for Gratte.
winterNote: Collab titles change every few weeks; check animatecafe.jp in Dec 2026 for Jan 2027 events. Some collabs need an online seat reservation, others are 'free entry'. Gratte at Animate Ikebukuro main store 10:00–20:00; numbered tickets when busy.

places.ja: アニメイトカフェ池袋
執事喫茶 スワロウテイル

anime: Changing official collabs (whatever runs in Jan 2027)

experience.hook: Drink a latte with your favourite character printed on the foam.
moments: Walk Otome Road past shops full of character goods and doujinshi.
Order a Gratte and photograph the character printed on the cream before it melts.
Eat a themed collab dish and get a random bonus coaster or card.
Browse the floors of the Animate Ikebukuro main store for goods.
experience.tip: Pick the collab first on animatecafe.jp, then check if it needs a timed reservation. Many collabs sell out on the first days.

title: Pokémon Café Tokyo, Nihonbashi
titleJa: ポケモンカフェ TOKYO
summary: The official Pokémon café in Nihonbashi Takashimaya. You eat Pokémon-shaped food, and Pikachu comes out for a short live show.
why: A playful, very photogenic meal for anime and game fans, with English and simplified Chinese menus.
cost: About ¥2,500–4,000 per person for a dish, a drink and a dessert (estimate; check menu).
winterNote: Reservation only, via the official site; opening time for bookings can change (it is usually about one month ahead, check the news page). Same-day seats only from cancellations at the door. Open 10:30–21:00, L.O. 20:30.

experience.hook: Pikachu walks out and dances beside your table.
moments: Go up to 5F of the Takashimaya East building near Tokyo Station.
Order a Pokémon-shaped dish and a souvenir-menu drink that comes with a café-only item.
Watch the Pikachu show, about 10 minutes long.
Buy café-only goods in the shop before your 90 minutes end.
experience.tip: Set a reminder for the day bookings open; slots go in minutes. Each email address can book only one slot.

title: Kirby Café at Tokyo Skytree
titleJa: カービィカフェ TOKYO
summary: The official Kirby café in Tokyo Solamachi at the foot of Skytree. Food and sweets look like Kirby and his friends.
why: Cute, funny food for game fans, and you can join it with the Skytree view.
cost: About ¥3,000–4,000 per person (estimate; check menu).
winterNote: Reservation needs an account (since Aug 2026 slots). Slots for a month opened on the 10th of the month before in 2026 (so Jan 2027 slots probably from about Dec 10, 2026, check). Max 3 bookings per month per shop; photo ID checked at the door. Open 10:00–22:00.

experience.hook: Eat a Kirby-shaped meal right under Tokyo Skytree.
moments: Find the café on Solamachi East Yard 4F, next to the Kirby Café The Store.
Order a Kirby dish and a dessert shaped like a Kirby character.
Photograph the food before you eat it; it looks too cute to cut.
Buy café-only goods at the store next door.
experience.tip: Come 10 minutes early with photo ID; the name on the booking must match.

title: Super Potato retro games and arcade
titleJa: スーパーポテト 秋葉原店
summary: A famous retro game shop on 3 floors with Famicom, Mega Drive and much more. The top floor is a small arcade with old cabinets and Japanese sweets (dagashi).
why: Old-school Japanese game culture next to the maid cafés; play a few ¥100 arcade games between cafés.
cost: Free to enter; arcade games from about ¥100; games and goods extra.
winterNote: Open every day 11:00–20:00. Kitabayashi Bldg 3F/4F/5F, next to the @home café main shop.

experience.hook: Walk into a shop packed floor to ceiling with Famicom cartridges.
moments: Go up to 3F and 4F, where the shelves are full of boxed retro games.
Look for old consoles, Famicom carts and rare handheld LSI games.
Play a round on an old arcade cabinet on 5F.
Buy a cheap dagashi sweet before you leave.
experience.tip: Check the back of the box for NTSC-J region before you buy a game to play at home.

title: Maid café night in Sapporo
titleJa: めいどりーみん 札幌狸小路店
summary: Maidreamin's 60-seat Sapporo shop on the covered Tanukikoji shopping street. Same maid show and spells as Akihabara, open until 23:00.
why: If you skip maid cafés in busy Tokyo, this is an easy, warm evening stop in snowy Sapporo.
cost: Entry ¥880 per hour + food/drink; about ¥1,500–3,500.
winterNote: Open daily 11:30–23:00. Tanukikoji is a covered arcade, so the walk is dry in snow. Sapporo Snow Festival 2027 dates: check (usually early Feb). Pin is Tanukikoji 4-chome (shop address: Minami 2-jo Nishi 4-10-2, Shimizu Bldg 6F).

experience.hook: Warm up from the Sapporo snow with a maid café spell.
moments: Walk the covered Tanukikoji arcade to the 4-chome block.
Take the lift to 6F of the Shimizu Building.
Chant 'moe moe kyun' over a hot drink with the maid.
Watch the stage show, then walk to Susukino for ramen.
experience.tip: Go after dinner; it is open to 23:00 and the evening shows are the liveliest.

title: Character latte at Animate Sendai
titleJa: アニメイトカフェグラッテ アニメイト仙台
summary: A small Gratte counter inside Animate Sendai, by Sendai Station. You drink a latte with an anime character printed on the cream and browse the anime shop.
why: A quick 30-minute anime stop in Sendai before or after gyutan dinner.
cost: About ¥1,000 per drink (check).
winterNote: Animate Sendai is in EBeanS 7F by Sendai Station, indoor. Gratte hours 11:00–19:00 (L.O. 18:45). Titles change; check the Gratte event list for Jan 25, 2027.

experience.hook: Drink a latte with an anime character printed on top.
moments: Walk from Sendai Station west exit to EBeanS and go up to 7F.
Choose a character from the current collab and order the Gratte.
Take a photo of the printed cream before you drink.
Browse the Animate shop for manga and character goods.
experience.tip: L.O. is 18:45, so do it before gyutan dinner, not after.

title: Kansai temples, food and Uji
titleJa: 京都・大阪・奈良・宇治
summary: D6 Shinkansen to Kyoto, Fushimi Inari at dusk · D7 Kinkakuji + Arashiyama (early morning for snow) · D8 Uji: Hibike! Euphonium spots + Byodoin + matcha · D9 Nara deer + Todaiji · D10 Osaka Dotonbori food · D11 Kobe beef + Arima Onsen · D12 fly KIX→New Chitose · D13 Otaru + Sapporo · D14 Sapporo, fly out. Or stop at D11 and fly home from Kansai (KIX).
why: Gives temples, food and one anime pilgrimage (Euphonium) with no long drives, and still ends in snowy Hokkaido if they want.
cost: transport approx. ¥35,000–55,000 pp (Tokyo→Kyoto Shinkansen ~¥14,200, local trains ~¥10,000, KIX→Chitose LCC ~¥8,000–20,000). Flight change: open-jaw, arrive Narita, leave from KIX (or CTS if the Hokkaido tail is kept). Loses Zao/Niseko skiing.
winterNote: Kyoto city gets settled snow only on a few days per winter (need 3–5 cm after a cold wave; go at opening time). Plan for cold, clear weather; snow is a bonus.
anime: Hibike! Euphonium (Uji Bridge, Daikichiyama lookout, Uji Shrine)

experience.hook: Golden temples, deer that bow, and the river town of Hibike! Euphonium.
moments: Walk up through thousands of orange torii gates at Fushimi Inari as the lanterns come on at dusk.
Stand at the Kinkaku-ji pond at opening time and see the gold pavilion, maybe with snow on its roof.
Climb to Uji's Daikichiyama lookout where Kumiko and Reina watched the town lights, then sip matcha by Uji Bridge.
Bow to the deer in Nara Park, feed them shika senbei, then face the huge bronze Buddha inside Todai-ji.
Eat hot takoyaki and kushikatsu under the Glico running-man sign in Dotonbori, then soak in Arima's rust-red gold water.
experience.tip: Check the Kyoto snow forecast the night before. If snow falls, be at the Kinkaku-ji gate for 9:00 opening, before it melts.

title: Japan Alps and Shirakawa-go loop
titleJa: 北陸・飛騨・信州 周遊
summary: D6 (Sun Jan 24) Shinkansen to Kanazawa, evening Shirakawa-go light-up (reservation) · D7 Takayama old town + Hida-Furukawa (Your Name) · D8 Takayama (Hyouka) → Matsumoto Castle · D9–10 Hakuba ski · D11 snow monkeys at Jigokudani + Shibu Onsen night · D12 Nagano → Tokyo · D13–14 Tokyo free days, fly from Tokyo.
why: Mixes two anime settings, a famous snow village, real Alps skiing for Pegasis and easy slopes for Aoki, and onsen monkeys.
cost: transport approx. ¥45,000–60,000 pp (Tokyo→Kanazawa ~¥14,400, Nohi buses Kanazawa–Shirakawa-go–Takayama ~¥6,000, Takayama→Matsumoto bus ~¥3,900, Nagano→Tokyo ~¥8,300, local buses). Light-up bus tours cost extra. Flight change: in and out of Tokyo; no Hokkaido.
winterNote: 2027 Shirakawa-go light-up: Jan 11, 17, 24, 31, 17:30–19:30, reservation only (parking from Sep 10 and Dec 1, lodging lottery Oct 1–31 2026, bus tours from Oct 13 2026). Jan 24 = baseline day 6. Jigokudani car road is closed in winter; walk 35 min from Kambayashi.
anime: Hyouka (Takayama town), Your Name (Hida-Furukawa station and library)

experience.hook: Snow-roofed farmhouses glowing at night, then monkeys in a hot spring.
moments: Stand at the Shirakawa-go viewpoint at night and look down on steep thatched roofs lit gold in deep snow.
Walk Takayama's old Sanmachi streets, the town behind Hyouka, and eat Hida beef sushi served on a rice cracker.
Stand on the footbridge at Hida-Furukawa Station, the same view Taki looks at in Your Name.
Ski Hakuba's big Alps runs while the beginner learns on gentle slopes in the same valley.
Walk a snowy forest path to Jigokudani and watch snow monkeys sit in steaming water, then hop Shibu Onsen's wooden public baths.
experience.tip: The Shirakawa-go light-up needs a reservation. Bus tour seats open Oct 13, 2026; book that day because they sell out.

title: Kyushu: Goto islands and onsen drive
titleJa: 九州：五島列島・阿蘇・別府
summary: D6 fly Haneda→Fukuoka, Hakata yatai stalls · D7 fly to Goto Fukue, rent car, Aokana spots (samurai street, Takahama Beach, Osezaki Lighthouse) · D8 Goto, fly back · D9 car to Kumamoto Castle · D10 Aso crater area + Milk Road → Kurokawa Onsen · D11 Yamanami Highway → Yufuin · D12 Beppu hells + sand bath · D13 back to Fukuoka · D14 fly home from Fukuoka.
why: Warmer roads let Aoki drive a lot, it has a rare anime island, and some of Japan's best onsen towns.
cost: transport approx. ¥60,000–85,000 pp (Haneda→Fukuoka ~¥12,000–30,000, Fukuoka⇄Fukue ~¥11,000 each way on ANA/ORC, rental car 6 days + fuel + tolls split by 2 ~¥30,000). Flight change: return from Fukuoka (FUK) — direct to Shanghai; Pegasis connects via Tokyo or Seoul. No skiing, no Hokkaido.
winterNote: Kyushu is mild (5–10 °C) but Aso and the Yamanami Highway can freeze or close after snow; ask the rental shop for snow tyres. Goto flights can cancel in strong winter wind.
anime: Aokana: Four Rhythm Across the Blue (Fukue Island, Goto)

experience.hook: Fly to the real Aokana island, then drive volcano roads between Japan's best onsen.
moments: Eat tonkotsu ramen and yakitori at a tiny Hakata yatai stall by the river on your first night.
Drive Fukue Island to Takahama Beach, the Aokana flying-circus practice bay, then hike 20 minutes to Osezaki Lighthouse at sunset.
Drive the Milk Road and Yamanami Highway across Aso's wide volcanic grass hills.
Soak in riverside rock baths in Kurokawa Onsen with a wooden tegata bath pass hung on your wrist.
Watch Beppu's boiling blue Umi Jigoku and red Chinoike Jigoku, then lie buried in hot sand.
experience.tip: In Fukue, stop first at Furusato Hall in the samurai district. It has the only Aokana display and the stamp rally items.

title: Hokkaido deep: drift ice and powder
titleJa: 北海道周遊：流氷とパウダースノー
summary: D6 fly Haneda→Memanbetsu, Abashiri · D7 icebreaker Aurora, drive to Shiretoko Utoro · D8 drift-ice walk at Utoro · D9 Lake Mashu, Kawayu Onsen, swans at Lake Kussharo · D10 red-crowned cranes at Tsurui/Kushiro → Tomamu · D11 Tomamu ski + Ice Village · D12 Furano ski · D13 Asahikawa zoo + Biei Blue Pond · D14 Sapporo, fly out (Tohoku skipped).
why: Pure snow country: drift ice, cranes, Hokkaido powder for Pegasis and wide easy runs for Aoki, with long snowy drives for Aoki.
cost: transport approx. ¥60,000–90,000 pp (Haneda→Memanbetsu ~¥15,000–30,000, rental car 8 days + one-way drop fee + fuel split by 2 ~¥45,000–55,000, Aurora ship ¥7,000). Flight change: none for home flights (still ends Sapporo); Zao, Sendai, Hakodate and Niseko drop out.
winterNote: Aurora icebreaker runs Jan 20–Mar 31 2027, but drift ice usually reaches Abashiri only around late January and is best in February; if no ice, the cruise still runs. Eastern Hokkaido roads are icy; long drives in the dark are risky.

places.ja: 流氷観光砕氷船おーろら
星野リゾート トマム

experience.hook: Break sea ice on a ship, float in it, then watch cranes dance in snow.
moments: Stand on the Aurora icebreaker deck at Abashiri and feel the hull crack through drift ice below you.
Put on a dry suit at Utoro and walk, jump and float on the frozen Sea of Okhotsk.
Dig in the warm sand at Lake Kussharo's Sunayu beach while wild whooper swans swim in the steaming water.
Watch red-crowned cranes call and dance on the snow at Tsurui, black and white against white fields.
Drink at the ice bar in Tomamu's Ice Village, then watch the Asahiyama zoo penguins walk through the snow.
experience.tip: Wear full ski wear on the Aurora deck. The wind off the ice is much colder than the town, and the best views are outside.

title: Tokyo base with day trips
titleJa: 東京拠点の日帰り旅
summary: D6 Shinkansen to GALA Yuzawa ski (station is at the ski base) · D7 Nikko Toshogu + Kegon Falls · D8 bus to Kusatsu Onsen, stay in a ryokan · D9 Kusatsu ski → Tokyo · D10 Kamakura + Enoshima (Slam Dunk crossing) · D11 Hakone onsen + ropeway · D12 GALA ski again or Kawagoe · D13 Tokyo shopping · D14 Tokyo, fly out. One hotel for most nights.
why: Least packing and moving, still gives ski days, onsen and Fuji views, and keeps Tokyo nights for anime and car meets.
cost: transport approx. ¥40,000–55,000 pp (GALA Yuzawa Shinkansen round trip ~¥14,000 x1–2, Nikko ~¥6,000, Kusatsu bus ~¥5,000 each way, Hakone Free Pass ~¥6,100, Kamakura ~¥2,000). Flight change: round trip to Tokyo only (simplest, cheapest flights).
winterNote: GALA Yuzawa usually opens mid-December to early May. Nikko roads above Kegon can be icy; trains and buses run.

experience.hook: One Tokyo hotel, but still ski, onsen, and Fuji views most days.
moments: Step off the Shinkansen at GALA Yuzawa and ride the gondola straight up; rentals are inside the station.
Find the Sleeping Cat and Three Wise Monkeys carvings at Nikko Toshogu, then see Kegon Falls hung with ice.
Watch the yumomi show at Kusatsu, where women stir 1.8 m boards to cool the hot spring water, then soak at Sainokawara.
Stand at Kamakurakoko-mae crossing as the green Enoden train passes the sea, the Slam Dunk opening shot.
Ride the Hakone Ropeway over steaming Owakudani and eat a black egg with Fuji in view.
experience.tip: Leave the big bags at the Tokyo hotel. Take only a daypack for the one night in Kusatsu.

title: JDM road trip: Izu to Gunma
titleJa: 伊豆・富士・信州・群馬 ドライブ旅
summary: D6 rent car in Tokyo, Izu Skyline + Shuzenji Onsen · D7 Fuji Motorsports Museum at Fuji Speedway → Kawaguchiko · D8 Yamanashi → Tateshina, ice-driving class at Lake Megami (booked event) · D9 Karuizawa → Ikaho, drive Haruna (Initial D Akina) in daylight · D10 Akagi view + Kusatsu Onsen · D11 back to Tokyo, return car · D12 guided JDM tour / Daikoku PA night · D13–14 Tokyo, fly out.
why: Most driving of all options for Aoki, real ice practice, Initial D roads and car museums, with onsen every night on the road.
cost: approx. ¥55,000–80,000 pp (4WD rental with studless tyres 6 days ~¥60,000–90,000, tolls ~¥20,000, fuel ~¥15,000, split by 2) + ice-driving event ~¥47,000 per car (2026 price, own car often required — check if rental cars are allowed). Flight change: in and out of Tokyo; no Hokkaido.
winterNote: Lake Megami ice sessions ran Jan 19–20 and Feb 6–7 in 2026; 2027 dates not yet found. Haruna and Akagi roads freeze in winter: studless tyres needed, go only in daylight and dry weather. Pegasis can drive normal rental cars (Times has no minimum years); only JDM sports-car shops need 3+ years.
anime: Initial D (Mt Haruna = Akina, Mt Akagi)

experience.hook: Drive Initial D's Akina, slide on a frozen lake, and sleep in onsen every night.
moments: Drive the Izu Skyline ridge road with Mt Fuji ahead, then soak in Shuzenji's hot spring town.
Stand next to the Mazda 787B Le Mans winner and Honda's first F1 winner at the Fuji Motorsports Museum.
Slide a car on the frozen Lake Megami in an ice-driving class and learn to catch it.
Drive the Mt Haruna hairpins, Takumi's Akina downhill, in daylight, then climb Ikaho's stone steps to a brown iron-water onsen.
Park at Daikoku PA on a weekend night and walk past tuned JDM cars under the highway loops.
experience.tip: Drive Haruna and Akagi before noon on a dry day. Shaded bends refreeze after sunset, even with studless tyres.

title: Shift dates for Sapporo Snow Festival
titleJa: さっぽろ雪まつりに合わせて日程変更
summary: Keep the baseline route but move it to Thu Jan 28 – Thu Feb 11 (15 days). D1–5 Tokyo/Fuji Jan 28–Feb 1 · D6–7 Zao + Sendai Feb 2–3 · D8 Hakodate Feb 4 · D9–10 Niseko Feb 5–6 · D11 Otaru Snow Light Path Feb 7 · D12–13 Asahikawa + Biei Feb 8–9 · D14 Sapporo Snow Festival Feb 10 · D15 fly home Feb 11.
why: Adds Japan's biggest winter festival and Otaru's candle festival, and drift ice and snow monsters are better in February.
cost: same transport as baseline; Sapporo/Otaru hotels during the festival are often 2–3x normal price, book early. Flight change: new dates only (in Narita, out New Chitose). Aoki's 15-day visa: Jan 28 – Feb 11 is exactly 15 days.
winterNote: 2027 Sapporo Snow Festival: Feb 4–11 (Odori, Susukino, Tsudome). Otaru Snow Light Path: Feb 6–13, 2027. Asahikawa Winter Festival 2027 confirmed for early Feb, exact dates not yet out. Chinese New Year is Feb 6, 2027: Shanghai flights and Japan crowds will peak.

experience.hook: Move the trip one week and get Japan's biggest snow festival plus Otaru's candle nights.
moments: Walk the Zao snow monsters at night, frozen trees lit in colour on the mountain top.
Walk 11 blocks of Odori Park past building-sized snow sculptures lit up at night.
See the ice sculptures on the Susukino street, then warm up with a bowl of Sapporo miso ramen.
Slide down big snow slides at the Tsudome venue in the daytime.
Walk the Otaru canal lined with snow lanterns and floating candles during the Snow Light Path.
experience.tip: Book Sapporo and Otaru hotels now: festival week prices go 2–3x, and Chinese New Year (Feb 6) adds crowds.

title: Hokkaido snow to Okinawa sun
titleJa: 北海道から沖縄へ
summary: Baseline to D11 (Otaru/Sapporo), then: D12 fly New Chitose→Naha, Kokusai-dori · D13 rental car north: Kouri Bridge, Churaumi Aquarium, early cherry blossoms at Yaedake · D14 Naha, Shurijo area + beach walk; fly home from Naha. Or skip Hokkaido and do Tokyo → Okinawa for D11–14.
why: A warm 17–20 °C ending after two weeks of snow, with an easy coast drive for Aoki and Japan's earliest sakura.
cost: transport approx. ¥25,000–45,000 pp (New Chitose→Naha direct ~¥15,000–35,000, rental car 2 days split by 2 ~¥8,000, Churaumi ¥2,180). Flight change: return from Naha (OKA) — direct to Shanghai; Pegasis connects via Tokyo. Loses Asahiyama zoo, Biei and Furano.
winterNote: Motobu Yaedake Sakura Festival started mid/late January in 2026 (extended to Feb 8); 2027 dates not yet announced. January also has humpback whale tours from Naha. Sea is too cold for most people to swim.

experience.hook: Leave minus 10 °C snow and land in 20 °C sun and pink cherry blossoms.
moments: Walk Kokusai-dori in a T-shirt, then pick fish downstairs at Makishi Market and have it cooked upstairs.
Drive across the long Kouri Bridge over bright turquoise water to Kouri Island.
Stand in front of the Kuroshio Sea tank at Churaumi Aquarium as whale sharks and manta rays swim past.
Walk under deep pink hikan-zakura on Yaedake, Japan's earliest cherry blossoms.
Eat Okinawa soba near Shurijo Castle, where the main hall is being rebuilt after the 2019 fire.
experience.tip: Enter Churaumi Aquarium after 16:00: the ticket is cheaper and the tour bus crowds have left.

title: Ginzan Onsen snowy night instead of Zao
titleJa: 銀山温泉
summary: Take the Yamagata Shinkansen to Oishida and see the old wooden ryokan street of Ginzan Onsen in snow and gas-lamp light at dusk. Stay the night in Tendo Onsen or Obanazawa, then Yamadera in the morning and Sendai gyutan in the evening.
why: It is the most famous snow night view in Tohoku (the 'Spirited Away' look that is huge on Xiaohongshu), and it keeps the onsen night without the ski day that is hard for Aoki.
cost: Tokyo–Oishida Shinkansen ~12,000 JPY one way; Ginzan shuttle 1,000–1,500 JPY; Tendo night tour 9,800 JPY; ryokan in Tendo 15,000–30,000 JPY with dinner
winterNote: Winter 2026–27 (Dec 2026–early Mar 2027): no private cars; day visitors park at Taisho Roman-kan and ride a timed shuttle (9:00–18:00, 1,000–1,500 JPY, stay about 1 h 20 min). Advance booking strongly recommended, same-day slots very few. Day visitors not allowed about 20:00–10:00. Easiest: Tendo Onsen 'Twilight Trip' tour, 12 Dec 2026–14 Mar 2027, 15:15 from Tendo, back ~19:15, 9,800 JPY incl. entry + fast pass. Ryokan rooms in Ginzan itself sell out very early.

experience.hook: Wooden ryokan, gas lamps and falling snow along a narrow river at dusk.
moments: Ride the Yamagata Shinkansen to Oishida and watch the snow get deeper outside the window.
Walk the short river street and eat a hot curry pan from Izu no Hana.
Walk up to Shirogane Falls at the end of the street, loud and half frozen.
Stand on a wooden bridge at dusk as the gas lamps come on and snow falls.
Climb the stone steps of Yamadera next morning, then eat thick gyutan in Sendai at night.
experience.tip: Book the Oishida shuttle bus early; winter evening entry is by reservation. Be on the bridges before sunset, about 16:50.

title: Yamadera mountain temple in snow
titleJa: 山寺（宝珠山立石寺）
summary: Climb about 1,000 stone steps through snowy cedar forest to temple halls on a cliff with a wide view of the valley. It is on the Senzan Line between Yamagata (20 min) and Sendai (about 1 h).
why: It fits the day 7 move from Zao/Yamagata to Sendai with no extra travel, and the snow view from Godaido is a classic Tohoku photo.
cost: Entry ~300 JPY; train Yamagata–Yamadera ~240 JPY, Yamadera–Sendai ~860 JPY
winterNote: Temple is open in winter but steps can be icy; wear shoes with grip or bring slip-on spikes. Some upper halls may close in bad weather. Opening hours in winter are shorter (check on site).

experience.hook: About 1,000 snowy stone steps up to temple halls hanging on a cliff.
moments: Step off the Senzan Line and walk across the river to the temple gate.
Climb through quiet cedar forest past the Semizuka stone of Basho's cicada haiku.
Stand on the Godaido balcony and look down on the white valley and tiny train line.
See the small red Nokyodo hall on its rock, the classic Yamadera photo.
Eat hot chikara konnyaku on a stick at the bottom to warm up.
experience.tip: Go in the morning before the crowds, and wear boots with grip. The steps are packed snow and ice in January.

title: Aomori and Hakkoda instead of Sendai
titleJa: 青森・八甲田
summary: After Zao on day 7, go north to Aomori (Sendai–Shin-Aomori about 1 h 30 min) for the Nebuta Museum and seafood. On day 8 take the bus to Hakkoda Ropeway for snow monsters and a Sukayu onsen bath, then a 1 h Shinkansen to Hakodate.
why: It shortens the long day 8 Hayabusa ride, gives a second, bigger snow-monster field, and Pegasis can ski Hakkoda's famous deep powder.
cost: Bus Aomori–ropeway 1,290 JPY one way; ropeway round trip ~2,500 JPY; Sukayu bath ~1,000 JPY; Nebuta Museum ~620 JPY
winterNote: Ropeway winter hours 9:00–15:40, stops in strong wind. JR Bus from Aomori Station runs only to Sukayu in winter (road beyond closed), ~80 min. Snow monsters are best Jan–Feb. Hakkoda is mostly ungroomed off-piste terrain: fine for Pegasis (a guide is advised off the course), not good for a beginner (Aoki can do snowshoe tour instead).

places.ja: ねぶたの家 ワ・ラッセ

experience.hook: Giant glowing Nebuta floats, snow monsters and a milky onsen, one hour from Hokkaido.
moments: Walk among full-size lit Nebuta festival floats at the Nebuta Museum Wa Rasse.
Build your own seafood bowl at Aomori Gyosai Center: buy tickets, pick sashimi stall by stall.
Ride the Hakkoda Ropeway up into a field of snow monsters, frozen trees in thick ice.
Soak in Sukayu's huge wooden bath with sour, milky water after the cold summit.
Take the Shinkansen from Shin-Aomori to Hokkaido in about one hour.
experience.tip: The ropeway stops in strong wind. Check its live camera in the morning and switch the Hakkoda and Sukayu order if needed.

title: Sukayu Onsen giant wooden bath
titleJa: 酸ヶ湯温泉
summary: A very old mountain onsen with the huge 'Sen-nin buro' wooden bath hall, milky acidic water, under some of the deepest snow in Japan. You can bathe as a day visitor or stay one night.
why: It is one of the most famous onsen in Japan, and the walls of snow around it look unreal in late January.
cost: Day bath ~1,000 JPY; stay ~12,000–20,000 JPY
winterNote: Open all winter; bus from Aomori Station ~70 min. The big bath is mixed (konyoku) with a women-only time slot; small separate baths also exist. Check women-only hours before you go.

experience.hook: One giant wooden bath hall, milky sour water, walls of snow outside.
moments: Ride the bus from Aomori Station up through high snow walls to the old wooden inn.
Walk into Sen-nin buro, a 160-tatami bath hall built all of hiba wood.
Try the different pools: hot, warm, and a hot waterfall that hits your shoulders.
Feel the sour water sting small cuts, then rest in the old lobby with a cold milk.
experience.tip: Rent or buy a yuami bath gown at the front desk for the mixed bath. Women also get a women-only time slot.

title: Oirase Gorge frozen waterfalls tour
titleJa: 奥入瀬渓流 氷瀑ツアー
summary: A guided bus and walk tour to the frozen waterfalls and ice pillars along the Oirase stream, with a night tour that lights up five ice falls. Best done with a night at the Oirase Keiryu Onsen area.
why: Blue-white ice falls lit at night are a rare winter sight, and it pairs well with an Aomori swap.
winterNote: 2025–26 ran 20 Dec–1 Mar, only Fri/Sat/Sun and New Year. In 2027, day 6 (Sun 24 Jan) fits; days 7–8 (Mon/Tue) do not. Meeting point depends on the course (Towada city, Oirase Keiryu Onsen, or Lake Towada for night tour); booking at frozen-oirase.com. Getting there without a car needs a hotel shuttle (e.g. from Hachinohe/Shin-Aomori) — check.

experience.hook: Blue ice falls and giant icicles along a snowy forest stream, lit at night.
moments: Ride the tour bus along the Oirase stream, black water between white snow banks.
Walk to frozen waterfalls and see blue-white ice pillars hanging from the cliffs.
Return after dark for the night tour when five ice falls glow under lights.
Soak in your hotel onsen by the stream to warm your frozen hands.
experience.tip: The tour runs only Friday to Sunday, so book the Sunday slot early. Wear snow boots; the paths are packed snow.

title: Stove train and snowy Hirosaki Castle
titleJa: 津軽鉄道ストーブ列車・弘前城
summary: Ride the Tsugaru Railway stove train from Tsugaru-Goshogawara, where staff grill dried squid on a coal stove, and see the tall Tachineputa floats and Dazai Osamu's house in Kanagi. In the afternoon walk Hirosaki Castle park in snow, then take the Shinkansen from Shin-Aomori to Hakodate.
why: It is a slow, local, very 'Showa' winter day with a unique train, a good contrast to ski days, and needs no driving.
duration: 1 day (needs night 7 in Aomori or Hirosaki)
cost: Stove train surcharge 1,000 JPY + fare; JR Aomori–Goshogawara/Hirosaki ~1,000–1,500 JPY; Tachineputa museum ~650 JPY
winterNote: Stove train runs 1 Dec 2026–31 Mar 2027, 3 round trips a day (times can change; tel 0173-34-2148). Hirosaki Castle Snow Lantern Festival is early Feb (2026: 6–11 Feb), so it is after this trip. Aomori–Goshogawara by JR is about 1 h+, Hirosaki–Shin-Aomori about 35 min.

experience.hook: A coal-stove train where staff grill dried squid for you in the snow.
moments: Look up at the 20-metre-plus Tachineputa floats in their tall hall in Goshogawara.
Ride the Tsugaru Railway stove train and eat squid grilled on the Daruma stove.
Walk Dazai Osamu's red-roofed family mansion, Shayokan, in Kanagi.
Walk the snowy Hirosaki Castle park and eat apple pie in town.
Take the Shinkansen from Shin-Aomori to Hakodate in the evening.
experience.tip: Only three stove trains run each day. Check the timetable first and sit near the stove; buy the squid onboard and a cup sake.

title: Kakunodate, Nyuto, Hakkoda rail loop
titleJa: 角館・乳頭温泉郷・八甲田
summary: Replace Zao and Sendai with a northern route: Tokyo to Kakunodate samurai street by Komachi (about 3 h), then bus to Nyuto Onsen for a night at a snowbound old inn. Next day Morioka (wanko soba) and on to Aomori or Sukayu, and on day 8 Hakkoda snow monsters before the 1 h train to Hakodate.
why: It gives the two most famous snowy onsen in north Japan and a second snow-monster field, all by train, and cuts the day 8 ride to Hokkaido to 1 h.
cost: Rail Tokyo–Kakunodate ~17,000 JPY; Nyuto inn 15,000–25,000 JPY with meals; Tazawako–Nyuto bus ~900 JPY; Tsurunoyu day bath ~700–800 JPY
winterNote: Nyuto: bus from Tazawako Station ~45 min; Tsurunoyu is reached by its own pick-up from Alpa Komakusa (booking needed). Tsurunoyu day bathing 10:00–15:00, outdoor bath closed on Mondays (day 7 = Mon 25 Jan 2027). Tsurunoyu rooms are hard to book; other Nyuto inns (Kyukamura, Taenoyu, Kuroyu may close in winter — check). Kakunodate and Yokote Kamakura festivals are mid-Feb, after the trip.

experience.hook: Samurai streets, a thatched onsen in deep snow, and snow monsters, all by train.
moments: Walk Kakunodate's samurai street, black wooden fences and snow on the weeping cherry branches.
Soak in Tsurunoyu's milky outdoor bath at Nyuto Onsen while snow falls and lamps glow.
Race to eat 100 bowls of wanko soba in Morioka on the way north.
Ride the Hakkoda Ropeway into the snow monster field, then soak at Sukayu.
Take the one-hour Shinkansen from Shin-Aomori to Hokkaido.
experience.tip: Book Tsurunoyu months ahead. If full, stay at another Nyuto inn; guests can buy a pass to bathe at all the inns.

title: Appi Kogen ski instead of Zao
titleJa: 安比高原スキー場
summary: Ski at Appi Kogen in Iwate, a big resort with dry snow, long groomed runs and good ski school, about 1 h by bus from Morioka. Then continue north on day 8 from Morioka on the Hayabusa.
why: It is better than Zao for a beginner like Aoki (wide gentle runs, lessons in English), still fun for Pegasis, and it is on the way to Hokkaido.
cost: Lift 1 day ~7,000–8,000 JPY; rental ~6,000 JPY; hotel 12,000–25,000 JPY; Tokyo–Morioka ~15,000 JPY
winterNote: Peak snow season in late January. Shuttle from Morioka Station to the resort; confirm 2026–27 times and if it is only for hotel guests. You lose the Zao snow monsters and Sendai gyutan (gyutan can be a station lunch box).

experience.hook: Dry Iwate powder and long wide runs: easy for beginners, fun for skiers.
moments: Take a morning group lesson at the ski school while your friend explores the upper runs.
Ride the Appi Gondola to the top of Mt Maemori and look out over white forest.
Ski the long Zailer course from the top to the base in one run.
Soak in a hotel onsen after skiing, then take the bus back to Morioka.
experience.tip: Book the Morioka to Appi shuttle bus online early. Reservations open before the season and buses can fill.

title: Morioka wanko soba lunch stop
titleJa: わんこそば（盛岡）
summary: Break the day 8 Hayabusa ride at Morioka for wanko soba, where staff keep refilling small bowls of soba until you close the lid. Most people eat 50–100 bowls; add Morioka reimen if still hungry.
why: It is a fun eating challenge that both can do together, and Morioka is a Hayabusa stop so it costs only about 2 h.
cost: Wanko soba ~4,000–5,000 JPY
winterNote: Open all year. Use the same rail ticket; take a later Hayabusa from Morioka (Morioka–Shin-Hakodate-Hokuto about 2 h). Busy at weekend lunch; day 8 is a Tuesday.

experience.hook: Staff keep throwing soba in your bowl until you slam the lid.
moments: Walk from Morioka Station to a wanko soba house like Azumaya.
Eat small bites of soba as the server drops in more and shouts to keep going.
Try the side dishes, like tuna sashimi and nameko mushrooms, between bowls.
Count your stacked bowls; reach 100 and get a certificate.
Eat cold, chewy Morioka reimen after if you still have room.
experience.tip: Drink no broth: pour it into the bucket and eat only noodles. Close the lid fast, or another bowl lands in it.

title: Matsushima bay or Hiraizumi temples
titleJa: 松島・平泉 中尊寺
summary: From Sendai, Matsushima bay with its pine islands and Zuiganji temple is 40 min on the Senseki Line. Or on day 8 stop at Ichinoseki for Hiraizumi's golden hall Chusonji (UNESCO), then take a later train north.
why: Easy culture and scenery near the baseline route for a slow half day after skiing; Matsushima also has fresh winter oysters.
cost: Chusonji ~1,000 JPY; Zuiganji ~700 JPY; Matsushima boat ~1,500 JPY; local trains ~400–600 JPY
winterNote: Both open in winter. Hiraizumi: Tohoku Shinkansen Sendai–Ichinoseki ~30 min (Yamabiko), then JR 8 min to Hiraizumi; most Hayabusa do not stop at Ichinoseki, so change at Sendai or Morioka.

experience.hook: Pine islands and winter oysters, or a temple hall covered in gold leaf.
moments: Ride the Senseki Line to Matsushima-Kaigan and take the boat through small pine islands.
Walk across the red bridge to Godaido, a small temple hall on its own rock.
See the carved rooms of Zuiganji, a national treasure temple.
Eat hot grilled oysters, fresh in their winter season.
Or walk the cedar path up to Chusonji's Konjikido, a hall covered in gold.
experience.tip: Pick one, not both. Matsushima fits a Sendai night; Hiraizumi fits the day 8 train north with a stop at Ichinoseki.

title: Aizu castle and Ouchi-juku in snow
titleJa: 鶴ヶ城・大内宿
summary: Go to Aizu-Wakamatsu (via Koriyama, about 2 h 40 min from Tokyo) for Tsuruga Castle in snow, then Ouchi-juku, a street of thatched-roof Edo inns buried in snow. Train fans can add a ride on the snowy Tadami Line to the First Tadami River Bridge viewpoint.
why: Samurai history and a thatched snow village are strong 'old Japan' images, different from ski resorts.
cost: Tokyo–Aizu ~9,000 JPY; castle ~410 JPY; Ouchi-juku taxi from Yunokami-Onsen station ~2,000–3,000 JPY per car
winterNote: Ouchi-juku Snow Festival is 2nd weekend of Feb (2026: 14–15 Feb), after this trip, but the village is snowy all of late Jan. Tadami Line has only a few trains a day (Aizu-Wakamatsu–Koide about 4.5 h); plan carefully, snow can stop trains. Day 7 returns to Sendai via Koriyama (~2 h). Replaces Zao ski.

experience.hook: A red-roofed samurai castle and a street of snow-buried thatched Edo inns.
moments: Walk around Tsuruga Castle, the only castle in Japan with red roof tiles, white with snow.
Eat sauce katsudon in Aizu-Wakamatsu, a local pork cutlet bowl.
Walk Ouchi-juku between thatched roofs heavy with snow.
Eat negi soba at Misawaya with one whole green leek as your chopstick.
Climb the steps at the top of the street for the classic view over all the roofs.
experience.tip: Ouchi-juku roads are icy; take a taxi from Yunokami-Onsen station and ask it to wait or book the return.

title: North Tohoku winter road trip
titleJa: 東北 冬ドライブ（盛岡〜青森）
summary: Aoki drives a 4WD rental with snow tyres from Morioka: Appi or Hachimantai, Nyuto Onsen, Lake Towada and Oirase, then over the Hakkoda snow walls to Sukayu and Aomori. Drop the car at Shin-Aomori and take the Shinkansen to Hakodate.
why: Aoki gets real snow driving, and the car reaches Oirase, Towada and Nyuto, which are slow by bus in winter.
cost: 4WD compact ~10,000–15,000 JPY/day + one-way drop fee (Morioka→Aomori, often several thousand JPY) + fuel
winterNote: Mountain roads in heavy snow and possible whiteouts; drive only in daylight. Hachimantai Aspite Line and the Towada–Hakkoda road beyond Sukayu (N103/N394 sections) close in winter; use open routes only and check road info (JARTIC) the day before. Both can drive a normal rental car; the more snow-experienced driver takes the mountain parts. Towada winter festival (2026: 30 Jan–23 Feb, closed Tue–Thu) starts after these dates.

experience.hook: Real snow driving past a frozen gorge, a caldera lake and Hakkoda's snow walls.
moments: Pick up a 4WD with studless tyres in Morioka and drive to Nyuto for a milky onsen night.
Stop by Lake Towada at Yasumiya, dark water under white mountains.
Drive slowly beside the Oirase stream and stop for frozen waterfalls on the cliffs.
Climb over Hakkoda between tall snow banks to soak in Sukayu's wooden bath.
Drop the car at Shin-Aomori and ride the Shinkansen to Hakodate.
experience.tip: Drive the mountain parts only in daylight, and fill fuel in towns. Check road closures on the prefecture site each morning.

title: Lake Towada Winter Story festival
titleJa: 十和田湖冬物語
summary: Snow sculptures, ice bars, light-up and small winter fireworks at 20:00 by Lake Towada at Yasumiya. It is one of the 'five snow festivals of Michinoku'.
why: Only relevant if the trip is moved later; it is a nice night event with a winter onsen stay.
cost: Free entry
winterNote: 2026 dates: 30 Jan–23 Feb, closed Tue–Thu, 16:00–20:30 (weekends 11:00–21:00). 2027 dates not yet announced, but it starts about late Jan, when the baseline is already in Hokkaido. Same for Hirosaki Snow Lantern (early Feb), Ouchi-juku (mid Feb), Yokote Kamakura (15–16 Feb).

experience.hook: Snow sculptures, an ice bar and winter fireworks over a quiet caldera lake.
moments: Walk between lit snow sculptures and snow huts at Yasumiya by Lake Towada.
Drink sake or hot drinks inside a bar built of snow.
Eat hot local food, like Towada barayaki, at the food stalls.
Stand by the lake at 20:00 for fireworks over the dark water.
experience.tip: Stay the night at a Yasumiya lodge; the last buses leave early. Check the 2027 dates; it is closed Tuesday to Thursday.

title: Grand Sumo New Year Tournament
titleJa: 大相撲一月場所（初場所）両国国技館
summary: The January Grand Sumo tournament runs Jan 10–24, 2027 at Ryogoku Kokugikan, so it is on during all Tokyo days. Go in the afternoon; the top-division bouts start at about 16:00 and end at 18:00.
why: It is only on 6 times a year in 3 cities, and your dates fall inside it by luck; it is a strong 'only in Japan' event for both of you.
cost: Chair seat 3,500–9,000 JPY weekday (C 3,500, B 5,000, A 8,000); box seat 8,500+ JPY; D seat 2,500 JPY
winterNote: Hatsu Basho 2027: Jan 10 (Sun) – Jan 24 (Sun). Advance tickets on sale Dec 5, 2026 (before the rankings are out). Jan 20–22 are weekdays (cheaper, easier). Jan 23 (Sat) and 24 (final day) sell out first.

experience.hook: Watch giant wrestlers slam together in two seconds, in a live 11,000-seat hall.
moments: Wait outside Ryogoku Kokugikan in the afternoon to see wrestlers walk in wearing kimono and hair topknots.
Eat the famous Kokugikan yakitori, made in the hall's own basement kitchen, from your seat.
Try a bowl of chanko nabe, the wrestlers' hot pot stew, sold in the basement.
Watch the top-division ring entry: wrestlers in silk aprons circle the ring, then the yokozuna does his stamping ritual.
Hear the crowd roar as wrestlers throw salt, stare each other down, and crash together.
experience.tip: Arrive around 14:00: lower-division bouts are quieter, and you can buy yakitori before the top bouts start near 16:00.

title: teamLab Planets and Toyosu footbath
titleJa: チームラボプラネッツ TOKYO DMM／豊洲 千客万来
summary: teamLab Planets is a digital art museum where you walk barefoot through water and light rooms. Next door, Toyosu Senkyaku Banrai has free rooftop footbaths with a view over Tokyo Bay, and a 24 h onsen (Manyo Club).
why: It is one of the top-ranked Tokyo spots on Xiaohongshu and Japanese blogs, and the onsen next door gives a first soak after the long flight.
cost: teamLab approx 3,600–4,800 JPY (price changes by date); footbath free; Manyo Club onsen 3,850 JPY + 150 JPY bath tax
winterNote: Indoor. teamLab Planets is extended to end of 2027. Manyo Club is open 24 h (bath closed 3:00–5:00); footbath garden 9:00–22:00. Book teamLab time slot in advance.

places.ja: チームラボプラネッツ

experience.hook: Walk barefoot through knee-deep water full of glowing digital koi.
moments: Take off your shoes, lock them away, and roll your trousers above the knee.
Wade through warm water while light koi swim around your legs and burst into flowers.
Lie back under the dome where flowers fall and spin above you.
Stand inside the Infinite Crystal Universe, a mirror room of hanging LED strings.
Walk to Toyosu Senkyaku Banrai and dip your feet in the free rooftop footbath over Tokyo Bay.
experience.tip: Wear shorts or loose trousers. After, soak at Manyo Club next door, with hot spring water trucked in from Hakone.

title: teamLab Borderless and Tokyo Tower
titleJa: チームラボボーダレス（麻布台ヒルズ）／東京タワー
summary: teamLab Borderless in Azabudai Hills is a large digital art museum where the art moves between rooms. Tokyo Tower is a 10-minute walk away; go at night when it is lit up.
why: A good alternative if you choose only one teamLab; it is dry (no water rooms) and the Tokyo Tower night view is a classic photo.
cost: teamLab 3,600–4,800 JPY (dynamic price); Tokyo Tower deck approx 1,500+ JPY (check)
winterNote: Indoor, permanent museum (opened Feb 2024). Timed tickets, book ahead. Most visitors stay 3–4 h.

places.ja: チームラボボーダレス

experience.hook: Art that walks between rooms, then Tokyo Tower glowing orange at night.
moments: Get lost on purpose in teamLab Borderless: there is no map, and the art moves from room to room.
Stand inside the Bubble Universe, a room of glowing spheres that repeat forever in mirrors.
Drink tea at EN Tea House, where digital flowers bloom inside your cup.
Walk ten minutes to Tokyo Tower after dark and see it lit warm orange above you.
Go up to the deck and see the city lights spread out in the cold, clear air.
experience.tip: Book an afternoon slot, stay about two hours, then reach Tokyo Tower just after the 17:00 sunset. No re-entry at teamLab.

title: Asakusa, Skytree and Yanaka old town
titleJa: 浅草寺・東京スカイツリー・谷中銀座
summary: Walk Senso-ji temple and Nakamise street in Asakusa, then see Tokyo Skytree across the river. Yanaka Ginza is a small old shopping street with snacks and cats, 'old Tokyo' feeling.
why: Asakusa is the top 'old Japan' spot for Chinese and Japanese visitors, and it is close to Ryogoku (sumo) and Kinshicho (day 2).
cost: Temple free; Skytree deck approx 2,000–3,500 JPY (check); snacks 1,000–2,000 JPY
winterNote: Open all year. Winter air is clear, so the Skytree has the best chance of a Mt Fuji view in the morning.

experience.hook: Old Tokyo temple smoke in the morning, the city from 350 m by afternoon.
moments: Walk under the giant red lantern of Kaminarimon gate to Senso-ji temple.
Wave incense smoke over your head at the big burner in front of the main hall, for good health.
Eat warm ningyo-yaki cakes and fried age-manju on Nakamise street.
Ride up Tokyo Skytree and look for Mt Fuji in the clear winter sky.
Walk down the Yuyake Dandan steps into Yanaka Ginza and eat a hot menchi-katsu.
experience.tip: Reach Senso-ji before 9:00 for photos with no crowds; Nakamise shops open later, so come back for snacks.

title: Tsukiji breakfast, Tsukishima monja
titleJa: 築地場外市場・月島もんじゃストリート
summary: Eat seafood bowls, tamagoyaki and grilled oysters at Tsukiji Outer Market in the morning. In the evening, cook monjayaki yourself on a hot plate on Tsukishima's monja street (70+ shops).
why: Chinese guides list both as must-eat Tokyo food, and both are cheap and fun for two people.
cost: Tsukiji 2,000–4,000 JPY; monja 1,500–3,000 JPY
winterNote: Tsukiji shops open early morning and many close by early afternoon; some close on Sundays and Wednesdays (check shop). Jan 20 is a Wednesday.

places.ja: 月島もんじゃストリート

experience.hook: Raw tuna for breakfast, then cook your own messy Tokyo pancake at night.
moments: Walk the narrow lanes of Tsukiji Outer Market while it is still cold and busy.
Eat sweet tamagoyaki on a stick and a grilled scallop hot off the fire.
Share a kaisendon bowl piled with tuna, salmon roe and uni.
At night on Tsukishima monja street, fry cabbage in a ring on the hot plate, then pour the batter inside.
Scrape crispy monja off the iron with a tiny spatula; try mentaiko, mochi and cheese.
experience.tip: Go to Tsukiji by 8:00 or 9:00. At the monja shop, ask the staff to cook the first one so you learn.

title: Shinjuku yakitori alleys and Golden Gai
titleJa: 思い出横丁・新宿ゴールデン街
summary: Eat yakitori and drink in the small smoky shops of Omoide Yokocho, then go to Golden Gai, 200 tiny bars in 6 narrow lanes. Both are a short walk from your Shinjuku hotel.
why: Easy first-night or last-night plan near the hotel, with no transport needed.
cost: 3,000–6,000 JPY; many Golden Gai bars charge a seat fee of 500–1,500 JPY
winterNote: Open all year, evenings. Some bars do not accept tourists or charge a cover; look for signs at the door.

experience.hook: Yakitori smoke, tiny bars with six seats, and Showa-era Tokyo alleys.
moments: Squeeze onto a stool in Omoide Yokocho and order skewers straight from the charcoal grill.
Drink a cold beer or highball while smoke drifts under the red lanterns.
Walk to Golden Gai and look through its six narrow lanes of tiny bars.
Pick a bar with an English sign, climb the steep stairs, and talk with the bartender and strangers.
experience.tip: Check the sign on each door for the seat fee. Have one drink per bar and move on to see several.

title: Tokyo public bath and sauna
titleJa: 黄金湯（墨田区）／小杉湯（高円寺）
summary: A sento is a local public bath. Koganeyu near Kinshicho is a modern sento with a very hot sauna and cold plunge; Kosugiyu in Koenji is a 1933 wooden bath with a Mt Fuji wall painting.
why: Koganeyu is 6 min from Kinshicho, already on day 2, so it is a cheap real Tokyo onsen-style end to the anime day.
cost: Bath 550 JPY; Koganeyu sauna +350–600 JPY
winterNote: Open all year. Check the weekly closing day on each official site before you go. Towels can be rented.
photoQuery: sento public bath Tokyo Mount Fuji mural

experience.hook: Hot sauna, ice-cold plunge, then craft beer while a DJ plays vinyl.
moments: Buy your ticket at the Koganeyu machine, near Kinshicho, and rent a towel.
Sweat in the wood sauna, then drop into the cold plunge. Repeat three times.
Soak in the high-carbonated bath and feel small bubbles cover your skin.
Sit at the bar counter by reception with a craft beer while the DJ plays records.
Or go to Kosugiyu in Koenji for its white milk bath under a painted Mt Fuji.
experience.tip: Wash fully before you enter any bath and keep the small towel out of the water. Weekday evenings are quieter.

title: Shibuya Nintendo, Pokemon and Harajuku
titleJa: 渋谷PARCO（Nintendo TOKYO・ポケモンセンターシブヤ）・竹下通り・明治神宮
summary: Before Shibuya Sky, visit Nintendo TOKYO and Pokemon Center Shibuya, both in Shibuya PARCO, plus Don Quijote and GiGO arcades nearby. Walk to Harajuku Takeshita Street and the quiet Meiji Jingu forest shrine.
why: It fills the day 5 afternoon near Shibuya Sky with game shops, arcades and a big shrine in one walk.
cost: Free entry; shopping budget
winterNote: All indoor except the shrine. Weekends (Jan 23 is Saturday) are very crowded at PARCO.

experience.hook: Nintendo, Pokemon and arcades in one building, then a quiet forest shrine.
moments: Browse Nintendo TOKYO in Shibuya PARCO for Mario and Zelda goods you cannot buy outside Japan.
See the life-size Mewtwo in its glass tank at Pokemon Center Shibuya, same floor.
Cross the Shibuya Scramble with thousands of people when all lights turn green.
Eat a crepe on crowded Takeshita Street in Harajuku.
Walk under the tall wooden torii into the silent Meiji Jingu forest and see the wall of sake barrels.
experience.tip: Book Shibuya Sky for about 30 minutes before sunset (near 17:00 in late January) to see day, sunset and night.

title: Yokohama Chinatown and Cup Noodles
titleJa: 横浜中華街・カップヌードルミュージアム横浜・赤レンガ倉庫
summary: Make your own Cup Noodle at the Cup Noodles Museum, walk the Red Brick Warehouse and Osanbashi pier, then eat in Chinatown. Minato Mirai is lit at night across the water.
why: Yokohama is next to Kawasaki and Daikoku PA, so it fits the day 3 afternoon before the car meet at night.
cost: Museum 500 JPY + My Cup Noodle 500 JPY; food 2,000–4,000 JPY
winterNote: Cup Noodles Museum is closed on Tuesdays (Jan 19 is Tuesday; Jan 21 Thursday is fine). Open 10:00–18:00, last entry 17:00.

places.ja: カップヌードルミュージアム横浜

experience.hook: Design your own Cup Noodle, then eat soup dumplings in Japan's biggest Chinatown.
moments: Draw your own design on a blank cup at the Cup Noodles Museum, then pick one soup and four toppings.
Watch staff seal your noodles and blow up an air-bag package to carry home.
Walk the Red Brick Warehouse and look for the outdoor winter ice rink.
Eat hot xiaolongbao and pan-fried shengjianbao on the street in Chinatown.
Stand on Osanbashi pier at night and see the Minato Mirai Ferris wheel lights over the water.
experience.tip: Get your My Cup Noodles Factory ticket first thing when you arrive; slots can fill on busy days.

title: Kamakura and Enoshima winter day
titleJa: 鎌倉・江の島
summary: See the Great Buddha and Tsurugaoka Hachimangu in Kamakura, ride the Enoden train along the sea, then walk Enoshima island. In clear winter air you can see Mt Fuji over the sea, and at night the Sea Candle tower has the 'Shonan no Hoseki' lights.
why: Winter is the best season for Fuji-over-the-sea views, and Chinese and Taiwanese guides rank it as the top day trip from Tokyo.
cost: Transport approx 2,000 JPY; Great Buddha 300 JPY; Sea Candle 800 JPY (+500 JPY garden after 17:00)
winterNote: Shonan no Hoseki 2025–26 ran Nov 22 – Feb 28; the 2026–27 edition is announced on the official site, dates for Jan 2027 not yet confirmed. Lights on from 17:30 after Jan 10. Fuji view needs a clear day (common in January).

places.ja: 江の島シーキャンドル

experience.hook: The Slam Dunk crossing, a giant bronze Buddha, and Mt Fuji over the sea.
moments: Stand before the Great Buddha of Kotoku-in, sitting outdoors for over 700 years.
Ride the small Enoden train by the sea and stop at the Slam Dunk crossing at Kamakurakokomae.
Watch the sun set behind Mt Fuji from Inamuragasaki cape.
Eat a shirasu whitebait bowl and a flat pressed octopus cracker on Enoshima.
Walk through Shonan no Hoseki: millions of LEDs around the Sea Candle tower at night.
experience.tip: Go to the Slam Dunk crossing early in the morning to avoid crowds. Lights start 17:30 after Jan 10.

title: Nikko shrines and frozen falls
titleJa: 日光東照宮・華厳滝・中禅寺湖
summary: Take the Tobu train from Asakusa to Nikko to see the gold Toshogu shrine in snow. Then take the bus up to Kegon Falls and Lake Chuzenji, where the small side falls freeze into ice.
why: A snowy World Heritage shrine and ice falls in one day from Tokyo, a good first taste of winter before Zao.
cost: Approx 6,000–9,000 JPY (train, bus, shrine, Kegon elevator); Tobu NIKKO PASS options (World Heritage Area 3,000 JPY; Oku-Nikko needs the ALL AREA pass, check price)
winterNote: The 12 small falls (十二滝) around Kegon usually freeze late Jan – early Feb; the main fall keeps flowing. Akechidaira Ropeway is closed Jan 16, 2026 – Aug 31, 2027. Irohazaka road can be icy; bus is safer.

experience.hook: A gold shrine under snow, and a 97 m waterfall with frozen side falls.
moments: Ride the Tobu express from Asakusa and watch the land turn white near Nikko.
Walk to the red Shinkyo bridge standing over a cold, fast river.
Find the Three Wise Monkeys, the Sleeping Cat, and the gold Yomeimon gate at Toshogu.
Take the elevator down to the Kegon Falls deck and see the ice beside the falling water.
Eat hot yuba (tofu skin), a Nikko special, to warm up.
experience.tip: Reach Toshogu near opening time, before tour groups. Take the bus up the Irohazaka road; it is icy for drivers.

title: Kusatsu Onsen night in snow
titleJa: 草津温泉 湯畑
summary: Kusatsu is one of Japan's most famous hot spring towns, with the steaming Yubatake in the centre and a big outdoor bath at Sainokawara. Watch the yumomi (water-stirring) show and stay one night in a ryokan.
why: It gives a real snow onsen town reachable by one direct bus from Shinjuku (your hotel area), no car needed.
cost: Bus approx 3,700+ JPY each way; ryokan approx 12,000–25,000 JPY per person with dinner
winterNote: Snow and ice from late Nov to April; bus runs in winter (safer than driving). Yumomi show about 6 times a day at Netsu-no-yu.

experience.hook: A steaming town square of hot water, and a giant outdoor bath in snow.
moments: Stand by the Yubatake and watch hot spring water steam through long wooden channels.
Watch the yumomi show at Netsu-no-yu: women sing and stir the hot water with long boards.
Soak in the big Sainokawara outdoor bath while snow falls on your head.
Eat warm onsen manju and a soft onsen egg on the street.
Walk back to the Yubatake at night when it is lit up in the snow.
experience.tip: Go to the yumomi show 15 minutes early for a front seat. Take off silver jewellery; the acidic water darkens it.

title: Yunishigawa snow hut lanterns
titleJa: 湯西川温泉 かまくら祭
summary: In a hidden onsen village in Nikko, hundreds of small snow huts (kamakura) with candles light the river bank at night. You stay in an onsen ryokan in the village.
why: A very photogenic winter night event, top on Japanese winter lists; but it probably starts after your Tokyo days.
cost: Heike no Sato 510 JPY; river lights free; ryokan approx 15,000–30,000 JPY per person
winterNote: 2026 edition: Jan 30 – Mar 1 (river-bank lights Fri–Sun only, 17:30–21:00). If 2027 is similar it starts about Jan 29, after days 1–5, so it does not fit the baseline. It only works if the trip order changes.

experience.hook: Hundreds of tiny snow huts with candles glow along a dark river.
moments: Walk Heike no Sato, a village of snow-covered thatched houses, with snow huts lit at dusk.
Stand on the Sawaguchi river bank as hundreds of mini kamakura light up at 17:30.
Slide down the snow at Mizu no Sato snow park, then soak in its onsen.
Eat dinner around an irori fire at your ryokan in the valley.
experience.tip: 2027 dates: Jan 29 – Feb 28. River lights only Friday to Sunday, 17:30–21:00. Book the ryokan early.

title: Mt Takao winter Fuji view
titleJa: 高尾山
summary: An easy mountain 50 minutes from Shinjuku by Keio train. Take the cable car halfway, walk past Yakuo-in temple to the top (599 m) and see Mt Fuji on a clear morning.
why: Cheap, short, easy for both, and winter is the clearest season for the Fuji view from the top.
cost: Train approx 400 JPY each way; cable car 490 JPY one-way / 980 JPY return
winterNote: Open all year; the path can be icy in the morning after snow. Go early for the clearest Fuji view.
photoQuery: Mount Takao summit Mount Fuji view

experience.hook: A short climb from Shinjuku to a clear view of snowy Mt Fuji.
moments: Ride the Keio line from Shinjuku to Takaosanguchi, about 50 minutes.
Take Japan's steepest cable car up to the halfway station in 6 minutes.
Walk past the Octopus Cedar and the tengu statues at Yakuo-in temple.
Stand on the 599 m summit and see Mt Fuji white against the blue sky.
Eat a bowl of tororo soba with grated mountain yam at the bottom.
experience.tip: Start before 9:00, since Fuji is clearest in the morning. Soak at Gokurakuyu onsen next to Takaosanguchi station after.

title: Kawagoe Little Edo old town
titleJa: 小江戸川越（時の鐘・菓子屋横丁）
summary: Kawagoe has old black clay warehouse streets, the wooden Toki no Kane bell tower and a candy alley. It is about 30 minutes by train from Ikebukuro.
why: An easy half day of 'Edo period' Japan with street food, without a long trip.
cost: Train approx 1,000 JPY return; food 1,000–2,000 JPY
winterNote: Open all year, outdoor walking; shops close around 17:00.

experience.hook: Walk Edo-period warehouse streets and eat sweet potato everything.
moments: Walk the Kurazukuri street of black clay warehouses built after a big fire in 1893.
Stand under the wooden Toki no Kane bell tower and hear it ring.
Buy old-style candy and a very long brown sugar fugashi stick in Kashiya Yokocho.
Eat Kawagoe's famous sweet potato as chips, soft-serve or warm roasted.
Try a COEDO craft beer, the local Kawagoe brewery.
experience.tip: The bell rings at 6:00, 12:00, 15:00 and 18:00: be at the tower at 15:00. Shops close near 17:00.
